(informal, usually, in the plural) Clipping of carbohydrate.
(organic compound) amino-formic acid, NH2COOH; it is too unstable to have been isolated, but its esters and salts are known.
A rifle with a short barrel.
(organic chemistry, nutrition) A sugar, starch, or cellulose that is a food source of energy for an animal or plant.

(uncountable) The chemical element (symbol C) with an atomic number of 6. It can be found in pure form for example as graphite, a black, shiny and very soft material, or diamond, a colourless, transparent, crystalline solid and the hardest known material.
(Internet) A duplicate copy of an email.
(inorganic compound) The normal oxide of carbon, CO₂; a colorless, odorless gas formed during respiration and combustion and consumed by plants during photosynthesis.
(inorganic compound) A colourless, odourless, flammable, highly toxic gas
(by extension) A spaghetti dish made using such a sauce.
Any salt or ester of carbonic acid.

(inorganic compound) A weak unstable acid, H2CO3, known only in solution, and as carbonate salts; it is present in carbonated drinks, and sparkling wine, but decomposes to form carbon dioxide and water.
(organic chemistry) A univalent functional group consisting of a carbonyl and a hydroxyl functional group (-CO.OH); characteristic of carboxylic acids.
(carboxylic acid) Any of a class of organic compounds containing a carboxyl functional group.
(US, Canada) A device in an internal combustion engine where fuel is vaporized and mixed with air prior to ignition. [from 1890s]

cit.quote: 尸身 屍身 尸体 屍體 尸首 屍首

sense.def: The body of a dead animal.
The body of a dead human, a corpse.
The framework of a structure, especially one not normally seen.
(formal, or, literary) Of or pertaining to imprisonment or a prison. [from late 16th c.]
A substance or agent that can cause cancer.
Causing or tending to cause cancer.
(countable) An invasive malignant tumour derived from epithelial tissue that tends to metastasize to other areas of the body.
Any flat, normally rectangular piece of stiff paper, plastic, etc.
(games) Any of the many games played with playing cards.
The seed of E. cardamomum, used as a medicine and spice, especially in curry powder.
(uncommon, inexact) , the seeds or seed capsules of Aframomum melegueta, of East Africa.
(biology, medicine) Pertaining to the heart.
(medicine, archaic) Exciting action in the heart, through the medium of the stomach; cordial; stimulant.
Of fundamental importance; crucial, pivotal.
(nautical) Of or relating to the cardinal directions (north, south, east and west).
Describing a "natural" number used to indicate quantity (e.g., zero, one, two, three), as opposed to an ordinal number indicating relative position.
Having a bright red color (from the color of a Catholic cardinal's cassock).

(Roman Catholic) One of the officials appointed by the pope in the Roman Catholic Church, ranking only below the pope and the patriarchs, constituting the special college which elects the pope. (See Wikipedia article on Catholic cardinals.)
Any of a genus of songbirds of the finch family, Cardinalis.
Any of various related passerine birds of the family Cardinalidae (See Wikipedia article on cardinals) and other similar birds that were once considered to be related.
(set theory, of a set) The number of elements a given set contains.
(geometry) An epicycloid with exactly one cusp; the plane curve with polar equation \rho = 1 + \cos\,\theta - approximately heart-shaped
(medicine) The study of the structure, function, and disorders of the heart.
A first aid procedure for cardiac arrest involving compression of the chest wall alternating with artificial respiration.
Cynara cardunculus, a prickly perennial plant related to the artichoke which has leaf stalks eaten as a vegetable.
Close attention; concern; responsibility.
(transitive, intransitive) To be concerned (about), to have an interest (in); to feel concern (about).
(intransitive, polite, formal, chiefly in the negative) To want, to desire; to like; to be inclined towards.
(intransitive) (with for) To look after or look out for.
(mail) For distribution by (the named intermediary).
(nautical, transitive) To heave a ship down on one side so as to expose the other, in order to clean it of barnacles and weed, or to repair it below the water line.
(nautical, intransitive) To tilt on one side.
One's calling in life; a person's occupation; one's profession.
(obsolete) A racecourse; the ground run over.
(obsolete) A short gallop of a horse. [16th–18th c.]
Conscientious and painstaking; meticulous.
Not giving sufficient attention or thought, especially concerning the avoidance of harm or mistakes. [from 16thc.]
Lack of care; the state or quality of being careless.
A gentle stroking or rubbing.
(transitive) To touch or kiss lovingly; to fondle.
An exponentiation symbol or operator ⟨＾⟩.
(chiefly, UK) Temporary, on a short term basis.
Someone who takes care of a place or thing; someone looking after a place, or responsible for keeping it in good repair.
(mainly North American) Someone who takes care of a person; a caregiver (UK) parent, carer or other guardian.
Freight carried by a ship, aircraft, or motor vehicle.
A ship that carries cargo.
Any of several North American subspecies of the reindeer, Rangifer tarandus.
Having the characteristics of a caricature, grotesque.
To represent someone in an exaggerated or distorted manner.
A person who draws caricatures.
The progressive destruction of bone or tooth by decay.
A purplish-red colour, resembling that pigment.
One of the teeth used by a carnivore for shearing flesh, being the last upper premolar and the first lower molar.
Of a rosy pink or red colour.
(botany) A type of Eurasian plant widely cultivated for its flowers.
The type of flower they bear, originally flesh-coloured, but since hybridizing found in a variety of colours.
A rosy pink colour
A festive occasion marked by parades and sometimes special foods and other entertainment.
(organic chemistry) A class of tetraterpene plant pigments; they vary in colour from yellow, through orange to red, this colour originating in a chain of alternating single and double bonds.
A continuously revolving device for item delivery.
Any of various freshwater fish of the family Cyprinidae; specifically the common carp, Cyprinus carpio.
A species of freshwater bream, Abramis brama.
Enjoy the present, make the most of today, (common mistranslation) seize the day.
A person skilled at carpentry, the trade of cutting and joining timber in order to construct buildings or other structures.

(nautical) A senior rating in ships responsible for all the woodwork onboard; in the days of sail, a warrant officer responsible for the hull, masts, spars and boats of a ship, and whose responsibility was to sound the well to see if the ship was making water.
(zoology) A carpenter bee.
A fabric used as a complete floor covering.
Large area bombardment done in a progressive manner to inflict damage in every part of a selected area of land.
A (mostly four-wheeled) lighter vehicle chiefly designed to transport people, generally drawn by horse power.
(now, _, rare) A manner of walking and moving in general; how one carries oneself, bearing, gait.
The key or lever that initiates the carriage return action (on a typewriter) or generates the carriage return character (on a computer).
Rotting flesh of a dead animal or person.
The common European black crow Corvus corone.
A vegetable with a nutritious, juicy, sweet root that is often orange in colour, Daucus carota, especially the subspecies sativus in the family Apiaceae.
A sweet cake, often iced, containing grated carrot.
(transitive) To lift (something) and take it to another place; to transport (something) by lifting.
(idiomatic, transitive) To take baggage or luggage onto an airplane, rather than check it.
(idiomatic) To behave, especially with respect to how one's speech, body language, facial expressions, and grooming convey one's opinion concerning oneself.
(transitive) To hold while moving it out.
(transitive) To execute or perform; to put into operation; to do.
A yoke of wood or bamboo, used by people to carry a load.
(economics) A group of businesses or nations that collude to limit competition within an industry or market.
(historical, politics) A combination of political groups (notably parties) for common action.

(skeleton, uncountable) A usually translucent and somewhat elastic, dense, nonvascular connective tissue found in various forms in the larynx and respiratory tract, in structures such as the external ear, and in the articulating surfaces of joints. It composes most of the skeleton of vertebrate embryos, being replaced by bone during ossification in the higher vertebrates.
(uncountable) The creation of charts and maps based on the layout of a territory's geography. [from 19th c.]
(comics) A humorous drawing, often with a caption, or a strip of such drawings.
(comics) A drawing satirising current public figures.
(arts) An artist's preliminary sketch.
(animation) An animated piece of film which is often but not exclusively humorous.
(firearms) The package consisting of the bullet, primer, and casing containing gunpowder; a round of ammunition.
(computing) A vessel which contains the ink or toner for a computer printer and can be easily replaced with another.
A gymnastic maneuver whereby the gymnast rotates to one side or the other while keeping arms and legs outstretched, spinning for one or more revolutions.
To shape to sculptural effect; to produce (a work) by cutting, or to cut (a material) into a finished work, especially with cuts that are curved rather than only straight slices.
To lay out; to contrive; to design; to plan.
The act or craft of producing a carved object.
A large knife designed for cutting cooked turkey and similar dishes.
A waterfall or series of small waterfalls.
An actual event, situation, or fact.
A piece of work, specifically defined within a profession; the set of tasks involved in addressing the situation of a specific person or event.
(academia) An instance or event as a topic of study.
(medicine) An instance of a specific condition or set of symptoms.
A box that contains or can contain a number of identical items of manufacture.
A piece of luggage that can be used to transport an apparatus such as a sewing machine.
A suitcase.
(legal) A legal proceeding; a lawsuit or prosecution.
A piece of furniture, constructed partially of transparent glass or plastic, within which items can be displayed.
The outer covering or framework of a piece of apparatus such as a computer.
(typography, by extension) The nature of a piece of alphabetic type, whether a “capital” (upper case) or “small” (lower case) letter.
Law developed by judges through court decisions and opinions, as distinct from statute and other legislation.
(uncountable) Money in the form of notes/bills and coins, as opposed to cheques/checks or electronic transactions.
A place in a restaurant, bar, or shop etc, typically containing a cash register, where a customer can pay the bill.
(figurative) To profit from something; to take advantage of an opportunity in order to profit, especially financially.
In a manner receiving direct payment by cash, often without paying tax.
A machine that tabulates the amount of sales transactions, makes a permanent and cumulative record of them, and has a drawer in which cash can be kept.
A box for holding cash.
A tree, Anacardium occidentale, native to northeastern Brazil, now widely grown in tropical climates for its cashew nuts and cashew apples.
The seed of the cashew tree, often viewed as a nut in the culinary sense.
Person in charge of the cash of a business or bank.
(mostly, uncountable) Fine, downy wool from beneath the outer hair of the Cashmere goat.
(mostly, uncountable) A soft fabric made of this wool.
That which encloses or encases.
A public building or room for gambling.
A large barrel for the storage of liquid, especially of alcoholic drinks. (See a diagram of cask sizes.)
(Britain) An urn.
A helmet.
(countable) A dish of glass or earthenware, with a lid, in which food is baked and sometimes served.
Food, such as a stew, cooked in such a dish.
The collective group of actors performing a play or production together. Contrasted with crew.
A supportive and immobilising device used to help mend broken bones.
The mould used to make cast objects.
A squint.
(of an animal) To throw off (the skin) as a process of growth; to shed the hair or fur of the coat. [from 15th c.]
(archaic) To give birth to (a child) prematurely; to miscarry. [from 15th c.]
(transitive) To assign a role in a play or performance to (an actor).
To turn (the balance or scale); to overbalance; hence, to make preponderate; to decide.
To perform, bring forth (a magical spell or enchantment).
To throw (light etc.) on or upon something, or in a given direction.
To shape (molten metal etc.) by pouring into a mould; to make (an object) in such a way. [from 15th c.]
To deposit (a ballot or voting paper); to formally register (one's vote). [from 19th c.]
A hard and brittle, but strong, alloy of iron, carbon, and silicon, formed by casting in a mould.
(intransitive, knitting) To finish the last row of knitted stitches and remove them securely from the needle.
(idiomatic, intransitive) To vote for something.
(musical instruments, chiefly, in the plural) A single handheld percussion instrument consisting of a pair of concave shells or shell-shaped parts joined on one edge by string.
Any of the hereditary social classes and subclasses of South Asian societies or similar found historically in other cultures.
A human tower formed in festivals in Catalonia.
Granulated sugar that has been sifted to have a finer crystal size, so that it can be shaken out of the holes of a caster.
(transitive, formal) To punish or reprimand someone severely.
(transitive, formal) To execrate or condemn something in a harsh manner, especially by public criticism.
(transitive, rare) To revise or make corrections to a publication.

A large residential building or compound that is fortified and contains many defences; in previous ages often inhabited by a nobleman or king. Also, a house or mansion with some of the architectural features of medieval castles.
A hat made from the fur of the beaver.
A male who has been castrated, especially a male whose testicles have been removed before puberty in order to retain his boyish voice.
Happening by chance.
(of clothing or utensils) Designed for informal or everyday use.
Something that happens by chance, especially an unfortunate event; an accident, a disaster.
(military) A person in military service who becomes unavailable for duty, for any reason (notably death, injury, illness, capture, or desertion).
An act seen as justifying or causing a war; an act of war.
A domesticated species (Felis catus) of feline animal, commonly kept as a house pet. [from 8thc.]
An animal of the family Felidae:
Any similar animal of the family Felidae, which includes lions, tigers, bobcats, leopards, cougars, cheetahs, caracals, lynxes, and other such non-domesticated species.
Carpobrotus edulis (Hottentot fig), a plant species in the Aizoaceae family
(nautical) A scourge (multi-tail whip) having nine, often knotted, whipcords, formerly used for flogging as naval punishment.
(biochemistry) Destructive (lytic) metabolism or metabolization, usually including the release of energy and breakdown of materials.
A platform used to display or convey a coffin during a funeral, often ornate.
A systematic list of books, names, pictures, etc.
(US) A book printed periodically by a college, university, or other institution that gives a definitive description of the institution, its history, courses and degrees offered, etc.
(music) A complete list of a recording artist's or a composer's songs.
(chemistry) The increase of the rate of a chemical reaction, induced by a catalyst.
(chemistry) A substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed in the process.
(figurative) Something that encourages progress or change.
(automotive) A chamber containing a finely divided platinum catalyst in which carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons from vehicle exhaust are oxidized to carbon dioxide.
(American spelling, Canadian spelling) That which catalyzes.
A twin-hulled ship or boat.
A boy or younger man in a homoerotic relationship with an older man. [1552]
A device or weapon for throwing or launching large objects.
A large waterfall; steep rapids in a river.
(pathology) A clouding of the lens in the eye leading to a decrease in vision.
(medicine) Inflammation of a mucous membrane.
Any large and disastrous event of great significance.
(narratology) The dramatic event that initiates the resolution of the plot; the dénouement.
(insurance) A disaster beyond expectations.
Of or pertaining to a catastrophe.
Disastrous; ruinous.
(uncountable) The game of catching a ball.
(countable, cricket, baseball) The act of catching a hit ball before it reaches the ground, resulting in an out.
(countable) A stopping mechanism, especially a clasp which stops something from opening.
(transitive) To capture or snare (someone or something which would rather escape). [from 13thc.]
(transitive) To entrap or trip up a person; to deceive. [from 14thc.]
(intransitive) To engage with some mechanism; to stick, to succeed in interacting with something or initiating some process.
(transitive, surfing) To contact a wave in such a way that one can ride it back to shore.
(transitive) To seize or intercept an object moving through the air (or, sometimes, some other medium). [from 16thc.]
(transitive) To grasp mentally: perceive and understand. [from 16thc.]
(idiomatic) To become engulfed in flames, to combust.
(ambitransitive) To reach something that had been ahead.
(often, attributive) Any structure or land feature which catches and holds water; the collection of such water.
(hydrology) A topographic region in which all water drains to a common outlet.
A book, in question and answer form, summarizing the basic principles of Christianity.
A group, often named or numbered, to which items are assigned based on similarity or defined criteria.

(mathematics) A collection of objects, together with a transitively closed collection of composable arrows between them, such that every object has an identity arrow, and such that arrow composition is associative.
A series of related items.

(engineering) Any physical cable, rope, chain, or other weight-supporting structure taking such geometric shape, as a suspension cable for a bridge or a power-transmission line or an arch for a bridge or roof.
The larva of a butterfly or moth; leafworm.
A vehicle with a caterpillar track; a crawler.
(maths) A set of subtrees of a tree.
A continuous track in the form of a steel or rubber belt fitted instead of wheels to crawlers, bulldozers, excavators, loaders, backhoes, tanks and similar off-road vehicles.

(drama) A release of emotional tension after an overwhelming vicarious experience, resulting in the purging or purification of the emotions, as through watching a dramatic production (especially a tragedy).
The principal church of an archbishop's/bishop's archdiocese/diocese which contains an episcopal throne.
(geometry) A line perpendicular to a surface (or line); in particular, either of the sides of a right triangle other than its hypotenuse.

(electricity) An electrode, of a cell or other electrically polarized device, through which a positive current of electricity flows outwards (and thus, electrons flow inwards). It can have either a negative or a positive voltage with respect to anode of the same polarized device (depending on whether the device is a load or a source, respectively).
The state or quality of being catholic or universal; catholicity.
(botany) A type of inflorescence, consisting of an axis with many unisexual apetalous flowers along its sides, as in the willow and poplar.
Any of the sharks in the family Scyliorhinidae
sly and spiteful; marked by malice
Certain other livestock, such as sheep, pigs or horses.
(pejorative, figuratively) People who resemble domesticated bovine animals in behavior or destiny.
(informal, of a person or remark) With subtle hostility in an effort to hurt, annoy, or upset, particularly among women.
(informal) Resembling or characteristic of a cat.
(fashion) A narrow elevated stage on which models parade.
(zoology) Pertaining to the tail or posterior or hind part of a body.
(zoology) Having a tail.
A large bowl-shaped pot used for boiling over an open flame.
Brassica oleracea var. botrytis, an annual variety of cabbage, of which the cluster of young flower stalks and buds is eaten as a vegetable.
The edible head or curd of a cauliflower plant.
The act of causing.
(countable, often with of, typically of adverse results) The source of, or reason for, an event or action; that which produces or effects a result.
(countable) A goal, aim or principle, especially one which transcends purely selfish ends.

A road that is raised so as to be above water, marshland, and similar low-lying obstacles, which in some cases may flood periodically (e.g. due to tides). Originally causeways were much like dykes, generally pierced to let water through, whereas many modern causeways are more like bridges or viaducts.
(of language, etc.) Sharp, bitter, cutting, biting, and sarcastic in a scathing way.
Prudence when faced with, or when expecting to face, danger; care taken in order to avoid risk or harm.
A careful attention to the probable effects of an act, in order that failure or harm may be avoided.
A story, originally told in folklore, to warn its audience of a certain danger.
(historical) A military man serving on horse, (chiefly) early modern cavalry officers who had abandoned the heavy armor of medieval knights.
(historical) A gallant: a sprightly young dashing military man.
(military, usually, _, historical, uncountable) The military arm of service that fights while riding horses.
A soldier in the cavalry.
A large, naturally-occurring cavity formed underground or in the face of a cliff or a hillside.
(uncountable) The activity of applying pigments to the interior surfaces of caves to create images, especially when carried out in prehistoric times.
A warning.
A large cave.
An underground chamber.
Roe of the sturgeon or of certain other large fish, considered a delicacy.
(anatomy) A hollow area within the body.
(dentistry) A small or large hole in a tooth caused by caries; often also a soft area adjacent to the hole also affected by caries.
(intransitive) To move about carelessly, playfully or boisterously.
(formal, intransitive) To stop.
(formal, transitive) To stop doing (something).
In warfare, an agreed end to hostilities for a specific purpose. (Typically only temporary).
(countable) A coniferous tree of the genus Cedrus in the family Pinaceae.
(architecture) The overhead interior surface that covers the upper limits of a room.
A pale green colour, possibly tinted with gray.
A pale green Chinese glaze.
A ceramic ware with a pale green glaze.
(transitive) To honour by rites, by ceremonies of joy and respect, or by refraining from ordinary business; to observe duly.
(intransitive) To engage in joyful activity in appreciation of an event.
(transitive) To perform or participate in, as a sacrament or solemn rite; to perform with appropriate rites.
famous or widely praised
A social gathering for entertainment and fun; a party.
A person who has a high degree of recognition by the general population for his or her success or accomplishments; a famous person. [from 19th c.]
A form of celery, Apium graveolens, having an aromatic taproot eaten as a vegetable. [from mid 18th century]
A European herb (Apium graveolens) of the carrot family.
(uncountable) The stalks of this herb eaten as a vegetable.
(musical instruments) A musical instrument consisting principally of a set of graduated steel plates struck with hammers that are activated by a keyboard.
of or related to Heaven and the divine.
Relating to the sky or outer space, regarded as the realm of the sun, moon, planets, and stars.
(astronomy, astrology) A natural object which is located outside of Earth's atmosphere, such as a comet, an asteroid, the Moon, a planet, the Sun, or a star.
(astronomy) A great circle on the celestial sphere, coincident with the plane of earth's Equator.
(astronomy) The dynamics of celestial bodies subject to mutual gravitational attraction.
(astronomy) The apparent outer limit of space; an abstract sphere of infinite radius which serves as the imaginary backdrop for celestial objects, and of which the visible sky is one hemisphere.
(mineral) A mineral with orthorhombic crystals, SrSO4, colourless or white with blue and sometimes red shades.
(chiefly religious) Not married. [from 1827]
One who is not married, especially one who has taken a religious vow not to get married, usually because of being a member of a religious community. [from 1869]
(obsolete) Specifically, any of the supposed compartments of the brain, formerly thought to be the source of specific mental capacities, knowledge, or memories. [14th–19th c.]
A device which stores electrical power; used either singly or together in batteries; the basic unit of a battery. [from 19th c.]
A small group of people forming part of a larger organization, often an outlawed one. [from 20th c.]
(entomology) An area of an insect wing bounded by veins.
(biology) The basic unit of a living organism, consisting of a quantity of protoplasm surrounded by a cell membrane, which is able to synthesize proteins and replicate itself. [from 19th c.]
An enclosed underground space, often under a building, used for storage or shelter.
(slang) Last place in a league or competition.
A large unfretted stringed instrument of the violin family with four strings tuned (lowest to highest) C-G-D-A and an endpin to support its weight, usually played with a bow.
Any of a variety of transparent plastic films, especially one made of processed cellulose.
Of, relating to, consisting of, or resembling a cell or cells.
The dimpled appearance of skin caused by the protrusion of subcutaneous adipose tissue, especially on a woman's hips and thighs.
(figuratively, often used attributively) The genre of cinema; film.

A complex carbohydrate that forms the main constituent of the cell wall in most plants and is important in the manufacture of numerous products, such as paper, textiles, pharmaceuticals, and explosives.
(uncountable) The paste-like substance resulting from mixing such a powder with water, or the rock-like substance that forms when it dries.
(uncountable) Any material with strong adhesive and cohesive properties such as binding agents, glues, grout.
(anatomy, dentistry) A bony substance that covers the root of a tooth; cement.
A monument, generally in the form of an empty tomb, erected to honour the dead whose bodies lie elsewhere, especially members of the armed forces who died in battle.

(transitive) To review for, and if necessary to remove or suppress, content from books, films, correspondence, and other media which is regarded as objectionable (for example, obscene, likely to incite violence, or sensitive).
The use of state or group power to control freedom of expression or press, such as passing laws to prevent media from being published or propagated.
An official count or enumeration of members of a population (not necessarily human), usually residents or citizens in a particular region, often done at regular intervals.
(money) A subunit of currency equal to one-hundredth of the main unit of currency in many countries. Symbol: ¢.
(money) A subunit of currency equal to one-hundredth of the euro.
(nuclear physics) A unit of reactivity equal to one hundredth of a dollar.
(Greek mythology) A mythical beast having a horse's body with a man's head and torso in place of the head and neck of the horse.
The hundredth anniversary of an event or happening.

(geometry) The point in the interior of any figure of any number of dimensions that has as its coordinates the arithmetic mean of the coordinates of all points on the perimeter of the figure (or of all points in the interior for a center of volume).
A place, especially a building or complex, set aside for some specified function or activity.
(historical) A former subunit of currency equal to one-hundredth of the franc.
A coin having face value of one centime.
(British spelling, Canadian spelling) (metrology) An SI unit of length equal to 10−2 metres. Symbol: cm
Being in the centre.
Being very important, or key to something.
Having or containing the centre of something.

(banking) The principal monetary authority of a polity or monetary union; it normally regulates the supply of money, issues currency and controls interest rates. It usually oversees banking activity within its country's borders.
The central area of a city in which there is a concentration of certain retail and business activities, especially in older cities with rail transportation.

(physics) In circular motion, the 'reactive' centrifugal force is a real force applied by the accelerating body that is equal and opposite to the centripetal force that is acting on the accelerating body.
(erroneous) Centripetal force.
(physics) The force on a rotating or orbiting body in the direction of the centre of rotation.

A period of 100 consecutive years; often specifically a numbered period with conventional start and end dates, e.g., the twentieth century, which stretches from (strictly) 1901 through 2000, or (informally) 1900 through 1999. The first century AD was from 1 to 100.

A Chinese delicacy made by preserving a duck, chicken or quail egg in a mixture of clay, ash, salt, quicklime and rice hulls for several weeks to several months, depending on the method of processing.
(pathology) headache
Of or relating to the cephalon (the head of a trilobite).
The fused head and thorax of spiders and crustaceans
(uncountable) A hard, brittle, inorganic, nonmetallic material, usually made from a material, such as clay, then firing it at a high temperature.
The art or science of making ceramic objects.
Ceramic objects as a group.
(countable) A type of grass (such as wheat, rice or oats) cultivated for its edible grains.
(uncountable) The grains of such a grass.

(neuroanatomy) Part of the hindbrain in vertebrates. In humans it lies between the brainstem and the back of the cerebrum and is formed of two lateral lobes and a median lobe. It plays an important role in sensory perception, motor output, balance and posture.
(anatomy, relational) Of, or relating to the brain, cerebrum, or cerebral cortex.
Intellectual rather than emotional or physical.
(neuroanatomy) One of the two regions of the brain that are delineated by the body's median plane.

(neuroanatomy) The principal and most anterior part of the brain in vertebrates, which is located in the front area of the skull and divided into two hemispheres, left and right, separated by a fissure. In humans it is the largest part of the brain and is responsible for the integration of complex sensory functions and the initiation and coordination of voluntary activity, and the higher mental functions such as consciousness, thought, reason, emotion, and memory.
A ceremony, or series of ceremonies, prescribed by ritual.
A ritual, with religious or cultural significance.
An official gathering to celebrate, commemorate, or otherwise mark some event.
A deep, bright red colour tinted with pink.
A chemical element (symbol Ce) with an atomic number of 58, a very soft, ductile, silvery-white metal that tarnishes when exposed to air.
Sure in one's mind, positive; absolutely confident in the truth of something.

(euphemism, preceded by "a") Used to denote that the speaker is referring to a specific person or thing that they do not want to name directly, implying that the listener should infer the identity of the referent.
Having been determined but not specified.
In a way which is certain; with certainty.
Without doubt, surely.
An emphatic affirmative answer; of course.
The state of being certain.
(informal, of a person) Mentally ill to such an extent that involuntary institutionalization is appropriate; crazy.
A document containing a certified statement.
The act of certifying.
(anatomy) Any of the seven vertebrae of the neck.
(now, specifically) The cervix uteri, or lower, narrow portion of the uterus where it joins with the top end of the vagina.

The ornamentation of fabric using needlework.
A piece of embroidered fabric.
In the reproductive cycle, the stage after the fertilization of the egg that precedes the development into a fetus.
The process by which an embryo is formed and develops.
The scientific study of embryos and (often) also the developmental biology of all prenatal phases (embryology sensu stricto plus fetology and teratology collectively).
Of a rich green colour.
Any of various green gemstones, especially a green transparent form of beryl, highly valued as a precious stone.
A rich green colour, like that of an emerald.
(intransitive) To come into view.
(intransitive, copulative) To come out of a situation, object or a liquid.
The act of rising out of a fluid, or coming forth from envelopment or concealment, or of rising into view; sudden uprising or appearance.
In particular: the arising of emergent structure in complex systems.
A situation which poses an immediate risk and which requires urgent attention.
An exit that is designed to allow rapid evacuation in the case of emergencies such as a fire.
The act of emigrating; movement of a person or persons out of a country or national region, for the purpose of permanent relocation of residence.
A body of emigrants; emigrants collectively.
Noteworthy, remarkable, great.
(of a person) Distinguished, important, noteworthy.

(legal, US, Philippines) The right of a government over the private property within its jurisdiction. Usually invoked to compel land owners to sell their property in preparation for a major construction project such as a freeway.
A prince, commander or other leader or ruler in an Islamic nation.
A country ruled by an emir.
Something which is emitted or sent out; issue.
The act of emitting; the act of sending forth or putting into circulation.

A digital graphic icon with a unique code point used to represent a concept, object, person, animal or place, originally used in Japanese text messaging but since adopted internationally in other contexts such as social media. Or, by extension, any non-standard emoji-like image inserted inline in text, i.e. an image emoticon.
(formal) Payment for employment or an office; compensation for a job, which is usually monetary.
A graphical representation of a particular emotion of the writer, used especially in SMS, email, or other electronic communication.
A person's internal state of being and involuntary physiological response to an object or a situation, based on or tied to physical state and sensory data.
Characterised by emotion.
(intransitive) to feel empathy for another person
Identification with or understanding of the thoughts, feelings, or emotional state of another person.
The capacity to understand another person's point of view or the result of such understanding.
Any monarch ruling an empire, irrespective of gender, with "empress" contrasting to mean the consort of an emperor.
The largest of penguins (Aptenodytes forsteri), that inhabits Antarctica.
Characterized by emphasis; forceful.
A political state, often a monarchy, that has achieved a much greater current size than its initial size by conquering surrounding territories, cities or nations.
A political unit ruled by an emperor or empress.
The group of states or other territories that owe allegiance to an imperial power (foreign to them), when distinguished from the native territory of that power; imperial possessions.
An expansive and powerful enterprise under the control of one person or group.
Pertaining to or based on experience (often, in contrast with having a basis in theoretical explanation) .

(philosophy) A doctrine which holds that the only or, at least, the most reliable source of human knowledge is experience, especially perception by means of the physical senses. (Often contrasted with rationalism.) [from 18th c.]
The state of being an employee; employment.
(obsolete) The act of employing someone or making use of something; employment.
To make busy; to preoccupy.
(uncountable) The state or quality of being employable.
A person who provides labor to a company or another person.
A person, firm or other entity which pays for or hires the services of another person.
The occupation or work for which one is used, and often paid.
The act of employing.
The state of being employed.
A purpose, a use.
The female monarch (ruler) of an empire.
The state or feeling of being empty.
Devoid of content; containing nothing or nobody; vacant.
(set theory) The unique set that contains no elements, denoted ∅ or {}.
(medical sign) A collection of pus within a naturally existing anatomical cavity (as opposed to an abscess, which occurs in a newly formed cavity).
A large flightless bird native to Australia, Dromaius novaehollandiae. [from 18th c.]
(computing) of a program or device: to imitate another program or device
A stable suspension of small droplets of one liquid in another with which it is immiscible.

sense.def: (chiefly, of a, trans, non-binary or cross-dressing person) Dressed in masculine clothing.
On the way.
Along the way.
(chiefly, electronics, computing) To activate, to make operational (especially of a function of an electronic or mechanical device).
(transitive) To act the part of; to play.
(transitive) To do; to effect.
An opaque, glassy coating baked onto metal or ceramic objects.
The hard covering on the exposed part of a tooth.
(mostly in the passive, followed by "of" or "with") To cause to be in love.
(neologism, informal) : a non-binary person; a person whose gender identity is not strictly female or male; one who is outside of the gender binary. [from 2013]
A campsite.
(pathology) Inflammation of the brain.
Something that enchants; a magical spell.
A woman, especially an attractive one, skilled at using magic; an alluring witch.
(transitive) To convert (plain text) into code.
(computing) The way in which symbols are mapped onto bytes, e.g. in the rendering of a particular font, or in the mapping from keyboard input into visual text.
(transitive) To include within its scope; to circumscribe or go round so as to surround; to enclose; to contain.
(transitive) To include completely; to describe fully or comprehensively.
A call or demand (as by continued applause) for a repeat performance.
A meeting, especially one that is unplanned or unexpected.
(transitive) To meet (someone) or find (something), especially unexpectedly.
To mentally support; to motivate, give courage, hope or spirit.
To spur on, strongly recommend.
An entry into a place or area that was previously uncommon; an advance beyond former borders; intrusion; incursion.
To conceal information by means of a code or cipher.
(cryptography) The process of obscuring information to make it unreadable without special knowledge, key files, or passwords.

A comprehensive reference work (often spanning several printed volumes) with articles (usually arranged in alphabetical order, or sometimes arranged by category) on a range of subjects, sometimes general, sometimes limited to a particular field.
(by extension) Death.
The most extreme point of an object, especially one that is longer than it is wide.
(transitive) To finish, terminate.
(copulative) To come to a final place, condition, or situation, sometimes unplanned or unexpected; to turn out.
(lutherie) In a violin-family instrument, the carved wooden plug which sits in the bottom block of the instrument.
Inspiring affection or love, often in a childlike way.
A sincere attempt; a determined or assiduous effort towards a specific goal; assiduous or persistent activity.
A disease affecting a number of people simultaneously, so as to show a distinct connection with certain localities.
A termination or conclusion.
The last part of something.
Having no end.
Extending indefinitely.
An annotation placed at the end of a document or chapter of a document.
(anatomy) Any of various glands that secrete hormones directly into the blood or lymph and not through a duct.
(physiology) The study of the endocrine glands of the human body, the hormones produced by them, and their related disorders.
One of the three tissue layers in the embryo of a metazoan animal. Through development, it will produce the digestive system of the adult.
(anatomy) The mucous membrane that lines the uterus in mammals and in which fertilized eggs are implanted.
To express support or approval, especially officially or publicly.
The act or quality of endorsing
An instrument used to examine a bodily orifice or canal, or a hollow organ.
(medicine) The examination of a bodily orifice, canal or organ using an endoscope.
Something with which a person or thing is endowed.
(music, lutherie) The spike of a cello or double bass that makes contact with the floor and supports the weight of the instrument.
To put on (a piece of clothing); to clothe (someone with something).
The measure of a person's stamina or persistence.
Ability to endure hardship.
To remain firm, as under trial or suffering; to suffer patiently or without yielding; to bear up under adversity; to hold out.
Someone who is hostile to, feels hatred towards, opposes the interests of, or intends injury to someone else.
A hostile force or nation; a fighting member of such a force or nation.
(attributive) Of, by, relating to, or belonging to an enemy.
(science) Possessing or pertaining to energy. [from 19th c.]
The impetus behind all motion and all activity.
The capacity to do work.
(physics) A quantity that denotes the ability to do work and is measured in a unit dimensioned in mass × distance²/time² (ML²/T²) or the equivalent.
A source from which useful energy can be extracted or recovered either directly or by means of a conversion or transformation process (e.g. solid fuels, liquid fuels, solar energy, biomass, etc.)
(transitive) To reduce strength or energy; debilitate.
(obsolete) To give force to; to strengthen; to invigorate; to urge with energy.
The act of enforcing; compulsion.
(transitive) To enter into conflict with (an enemy).
Having agreed to marry a particular person (one's fiancé or fiancée) or each other.
(transitive) To bring into existence (a situation, quality, result etc.); to give rise to, cause, create. [from 14th c.]
(intransitive) To assume form; to come into existence; to be caused or produced.
A complex mechanical device which converts energy into useful motion or physical effects. [from 16th c.]
problems occurring with an engine or motor, especially with that of a motor car

Originally, a person engaged in designing, constructing, or maintaining engines or machinery; now (more generally) , a person qualified or professionally engaged in any branch of engineering, or studying to do so.
(uncountable) The application of mathematics and the physical sciences to the needs of humanity and the development of technology.

To improve something by adding features.

A riddle, or a difficult problem.

It causes constriction of the blood vessels and widening of the bronchial passages and is used in the form of its hydrochloride or sulfate to relieve asthma and hay fever.

Of horseback riding or horseback riders.

Of or relating to a horse or horses.

A natural celestial object, visible in the sky, such as a star, planet, natural satellite, asteroid, comet, the Moon or the Sun. Objects flying or moving in the atmosphere are not usually considered as heavenly bodies.
One of the ten terms used in East Asian cultures to represent

A small mammal, of the family Erinaceidae or subfamily Erinaceinae (spiny hedgehogs, the latter characterized by their spiny back and often by the habit of rolling up into a ball when attacked.)

In particular, of or relating to a people (or their language or culture) that inhabited a region prior to the arrival of people of other cultures which became dominant (e.g., through colonialism), and which maintains a distinct culture.
Poor; destitute; in need.
Difficult or impossible to digest.
An anger aroused by something perceived as an indignity, notably an offense or injustice.
A self-righteous anger or disgust.
having a deep purplish-blue colour
A purplish-blue colour.
An indigo-colored dye obtained from certain plants (indigo plant or woad), or a similar synthetic dye.
A blue bunting of North America (Passerina cyanea).
Not direct:
Not discreet; lacking in discretion.
Not disputable; not open to question; obviously true
A chemical element (symbol In) with an atomic number of 49: a soft silvery-white metal.
Relating to a single person or thing as opposed to more than one.
Intended for a single person as opposed to more than one person.
A person considered alone, rather than as belonging to a group of people.
(legal) A single physical human being as a legal subject, as opposed to a legal person such as a corporation.
The tendency for a person to act without reference to others, particularly in matters of style, fashion or mode of thought.

The moral stance, political philosophy, or social outlook that promotes independence and self-reliance of individual people, while opposing the interference with each person's choices by society, the state, or any other group or institution.
To teach with a biased, one-sided or uncritical ideology; to brainwash.

(organic compound) An organic compound, C8H7N, found in coal tar, and produced in the gut by the bacterial decomposition of tryptophan; it is an aromatic bicyclic heterocycle having a benzene ring fused with a pyrrole ring; indole and its derivatives occur widely in nature and have many industrial applications.
(organic compound) Any of the derivatives of indole.
Habitually lazy, procrastinating, or resistant to physical labor
(medicine) Causing little or no physical pain; progressing slowly; inactive (of an ulcer, etc.)
Inside, into, or within a building.
(embryology) Given a group of cells that emits or displays a substance, the influence of this substance on the fate of a second group of cells
(physics) Generation of an electric current by a varying magnetic field.
(electronics) A passive device that introduces inductance into an electrical circuit.
The act of indulging.
Something in which someone indulges.
Of or relating to industry, notably manufacturing.
The socioeconomic system based upon the industrial production of manufactured goods, rather than on agriculture.
Hard-working and persistent.
(uncountable, economics) Businesses that produce goods as opposed to services.
The state or characteristic of drunkenness.
Forbidden to be uttered; taboo.
Unable or insufficient to produce effect.
Worthless; ineffective.
Weak, indecisive; lacking forcefulness.
Not efficient; not producing the effect intended or desired; inefficacious
Impossible to avoid or escape; inescapable, irresistible.
Not able to do something; not proficient; displaying incompetence.
The quality of being inept.
An unfair, not equal, state.
(mathematics) A statement that of two quantities one is specifically less than (or greater than) another. Symbol: < or \leq or > or \geq or \ne, as appropriate.
(figuratively) In a person, unwillingness to take action.
low in price
Impossible to explain; not easily accounted for.
Impossible to eliminate or destroy; impregnable.
The property of being infallible; the ability to never make a mistake.
Without fault or weakness; incapable of error or fallacy.

(UK, historical) Subject to a judicial punishment that deprived the infamous person of certain rights; this included a prohibition against holding public office, exercising the franchise, receiving a public pension, serving on a jury, or giving testimony in a court of law.
A very young human being, from birth to somewhere between six months and two years of age after birth, needing almost constant care and attention.
(legal) A minor.
(law, Canada) The criminal offence of killing of a newborn, committed by its mother while psychologically disturbed by the effects of childbirth or lactation, not regarded as murder.
Soldiers who fight on foot (on land), as opposed to cavalry and other mounted units, regardless of external transport (e.g. airborne).
(uncountable) The part of an army consisting of infantry soldiers, especially opposed to mounted and technical troops.
(military) a soldier employed in an infantry role
(by restriction) a male soldier of the infantry
An immensely strong love or sexual attraction.
(obsolete) The act of infatuating; the state of being infatuated; madness.

(transitive) To bring (the body or part of it) into contact with a substance that causes illness (a pathogen), so that the pathogen begins to act on the body; (of a pathogen) to come into contact with (a body or body part) and begin to act on it.
(pathology) The act or process of infecting.
An uncontrolled growth of harmful microorganisms in a host.

(medicine) An illness caused by a specific infectious agent (bacterium, virus, fungus, protozoa, prion etc.), that results from transmission of that agent from an infected person, animal, or reservoir to a susceptible host.
(medicine) A medical specialty dealing with the diagnosis, control and treatment of infections.
Inappropriate or awkward; not well said, expressed, or done.
(transitive) To introduce (something) as a reasoned conclusion; to conclude by reasoning or deduction, as from premises or evidence. [from 16th c.]
(uncountable) The act or process of inferring by deduction or induction.
Of low rank, standard or quality.
Of or relating to hell, or the world of the dead; hellish.
A place or situation resembling Hell.
A large fire; a conflagration.
Not fertile.
Indefinably large, countlessly great; immense. [from 14th c.]
Boundless, endless, without end or limits; innumerable. [from 15th c.]
(mathematics) Greater than any positive quantity or magnitude; limitless. [from 17th c.]
In an infinite manner; as of anything growing without bounds; endlessly.

(grammar) A non-finite verb form considered neutral with respect to inflection; depending on language variously found used with auxiliary verbs, in subordinate clauses, or acting as a gerund, and often as the dictionary form.
(uncountable) endlessness, unlimitedness, absence of a beginning, end or limits to size.

(uncountable) A number which is very large compared to some characteristic number. For example, in optics, an object which is much further away than the focal length of a lens is said to be "at infinity", as the distance of the image from the lens varies very little as the distance increases further.
A place where sick or injured people are cared for, especially a small hospital; sickhouse.
(transitive) To set on fire; to kindle; to cause to burn, flame, or glow.
Capable of burning; easily set on fire.

(pathology) A condition of any part of the body, consisting of congestion of the blood vessels, with obstruction of the blood current, and growth of morbid tissue. It is manifested outwardly by redness and swelling, attended with heat and pain.
Able to be inflated or blown up.
(transitive) To enlarge an object by pushing air (or a gas) into it; to raise or expand abnormally
(economics) An increase in the general level of prices or in the cost of living.
(linguistics) That can be inflected.
(grammar, uncountable) A change in the form of a word (morphologic change) to express different grammatical categories.
A turning away from a straight course.
Not flexible; not capable of bending or being bent.
Not willing to change, e.g. one's opinion or habits.
Not able to be changed or adapted to circumstances.
(botany) Flower cluster; a group or cluster of flowers arranged on a stem that is composed of a main branch or a complicated arrangement of branches.
The power to affect, control or manipulate something or someone; the ability to change the development of fluctuating things such as conduct, thoughts or decisions.
An action exerted by a person or thing with such power on another to cause change.
A person or thing exerting such power or action.
(transitive) To have an effect on by using gentle or subtle action; to exert an influence upon; to modify, bias, or sway; to persuade or induce.

(social media, marketing) A person who is able to influence consumption, lifestyle, and/or political preferences of their online audience by creating and/or engaging social media content, often as a part of a marketing campaign.
(disease) An acute contagious disease of the upper airways and lungs, caused by a virus, which rapidly spreads around the world in seasonal epidemics.
(transitive) To give form or character to; to inspire (with a given quality); to affect, influence (with a pervading principle, idea etc.).
Not formal or ceremonious.
Not in accord with the usual regulations.
(of language) Reflecting everyday, non-ceremonious usage.
One who relays confidential information to someone, especially to the police; an informer.

(computing) A branch of information science and of computer science that focuses on the study of information processing, particularly with respect to systems integration and human interactions with machine and data.
Things that are or can be known about a given topic; communicable knowledge of something. [from 14th c.]
(sociology) A society where the creation, distribution, use, integration and manipulation of information is a significant economic, political, and cultural activity.
Any data processing system, either manual or computerized.
(computing) The practice of creating and/or studying computer systems and applications.
below, beneath, inferior
Having a wavelength in the infrared spectrum.
(uncountable) The electromagnetic radiation of a wavelength longer than visible light, but shorter than microwave radiation, having a wavelength between 700 nm and 1 mm.
(physics) Sound waves having a frequency below the human audible range (below about 20 Hz).
(systems theory) An underlying base or foundation especially for an organization or system. [from 1887]
The basic facilities, services and installations needed for the functioning of a community or society.
Not frequent; not happening frequently.
(botany) The fruiting stage of an inflorescence
One of the substances present in a mixture, especially food.
The act of entering.
A door or other means of entering.
(astronomy) The entrance of the Moon into the shadow of the Earth in eclipses, or the Sun's entrance into a sign, etc.
(transitive) To live or reside in.
(transitive) To be present in.
Someone or thing who lives in a place.

(transitive) To draw air or any form of gas (either in a pure form, or mixed with small particles in form of aerosols/smoke -sometimes stemming from a medicament) into the lungs, through the nose or mouth by action of the diaphragm.
Naturally as part or consequence of something.
(transitive) To receive (property, a title, etc.), by legal succession or bequest after the previous owner's death.
The passing of title to an estate upon death.
(biology, genetic algorithms) The biological attributes passed hereditarily from ancestors to their offspring.
(programming, object-oriented) The mechanism whereby parts of a superclass are available to instances of its subclass.

Unfriendly, hostile.
Spatially first, placed at the beginning, in the first position; especially said of the first letter of a word.
(linguistics) A term formed from the initial letters of several words or parts of words, which is itself pronounced letter by letter.
(transitive) To administer an injection to (someone or something), especially of medicine or drugs.
The act of injecting, or something that is injected.
(transitive) To wound or cause physical harm to a living creature.
The violation of a person's reputation, rights, property, or interests.
A pigment (or dye)-based fluid used for writing, printing etc.
The black or dark-colored fluid ejected by squid, octopus etc, as a protective strategy.
(used attributively, pejorative, of vocabulary) Pedantic, obscurely scholarly.
Usually preceded by forms of to give: a slight hint, implication, or suggestion given.
Often preceded by forms of to get or to have: an imprecise idea or slight knowledge of something; a suspicion.
A container for ink, designed and usually positioned so that a person may conveniently dip a pen into it whenever a refill is needed.
The material placed within a different material in the form of a decoration.
(dentistry) A filling for a tooth, made of ceramic or gold to fit the cavity and shape of tooth and cemented into place.
Any establishment where travellers can procure lodging, food, and drink.
(urban studies) The central part of a city, especially an older, populous area of low-income or immigrant families as opposed to centrally-located commercial areas.
(anatomy) The portion of the ear located within the temporal bone which includes the semicircular canals, vestibule, and cochlea and is responsible for hearing and balance.

(baseball) A period of play in which members of a visiting baseball team attempt to hit a baseball pitched by the opposing home team until three players are called out, followed by a similar attempt by members of the home baseball team against the visiting team's pitching. There are nine or more innings in a regulation baseball game.
Free from guilt, sin, or immorality.
Bearing no legal responsibility for a wrongful act.
Without wrongful intent; accidental or in good faith.
Naive; artless.
Harmless; producing no ill effect.
Having no name, nameless, unnamed; anonymous.

The act of innovating; the introduction of something new, in customs, rites, etc.
Something new, and contrary to established customs, manners, or rites.
(immunology) The introduction of an antigenic substance or vaccine into the body to produce immunity to a specific disease.
(chemistry) relating to a compound that does not contain carbon
(chemistry) The chemistry of the elements (including carbon), and those compounds that do not contain carbon.
Contribution of work or information, as an opinion or advice.
Data fed into a process with the intention of it shaping or affecting the output of that process.

The act of inquiring; a seeking of information by asking questions; interrogation; a question or questioning.
Search for truth, information, or knowledge; examination of facts or principles; research; investigation
The quality of being inquisitive; curiosity.
Exhibiting unsoundness or disorder of mind; not sane; utterly mad.

The state of being insane; madness.

The text on a coin.
Difficult or impossible to comprehend, fathom, or interpret.

(colloquial) Any small arthropod similar to an insect, including spiders, centipedes, millipedes, etc.
(derogatory) A contemptible or powerless person.

The introduction of sperm into a female’s reproductive system for the purpose of impregnating (making pregnant).
An image inserted into text.
A promotional or instructive leaflet inserted into a magazine, newspaper, tape or disk package, etc.

Within or towards the interior of something; within the scope or limits of something (a place), especially a building.
The interior or inner part.
The side of a curved road, racetrack etc. that has the shorter arc length; the side of a racetrack nearer the interior of the course or some other point of reference.
Within the interior of something, closest to the center or to a specific point of reference.
(idiomatic) A joke that is understood or meant to be understood only by certain people who are aware of the details (an ingroup).

sense.def: Producing harm in a stealthy, often gradual, manner.
A sight or view of the interior of anything; a deep inspection or view; introspection; frequently used with into.
To hint; to suggest tacitly (usually something bad) while avoiding a direct statement.
(figurative, by extension) To ingratiate; to obtain access to or introduce something by subtle, cunning or artful means.
(with on or upon or (that + indicative)) To hold up a claim emphatically.
to the extent that
Contemptible, ill-mannered conduct; insulting: arrogant, bold behaviour or attitude.

An organization that checks that certain laws or rules are obeyed.

One of a series of recurring occasions, cases, essentially the same.
(legal) Present; current; extant.
Occurring immediately; immediate; present.
A very short period of time; a moment.
A single, usually precise, point in time.
A beverage in the form of a powder, granules, or concentrated liquid, made from coffee and able to be quickly reconstituted by adding water.
(chiefly, in the plural) One of a mass of dried precooked noodles fused with oil, usually soaked in boiling water for a few minutes before being eaten.
Occurring, arising, or functioning without any delay; happening within an imperceptibly brief period of time. [from 17th c.]
Without any delay; in an instantaneous manner.
At once; without delay. [from 16th c.]
An arthropod at a specified one of these stages of development.
In the place of something (usually mentioned earlier); as a substitute or alternative.
In lieu of; in place of; rather than.
A natural or inherent impulse or behaviour.
Innately; by instinct; without being taught.
An institution of learning; a college, especially for technical subjects
A custom or practice of a society or community.
A long established and respected organization, particularly one involved with education, public service, or charity work.
(transitive) To teach by giving instructions.
(uncountable) The act of instructing, teaching, or providing with information or knowledge.

A device used to produce music.
A measuring or displaying device.
A tool, implement used for manipulation or measurement.

The lack of sufficiency; a shortage or inadequacy.
not sufficiently
Situated on an island.

(linguistics, anthropology) (often with a capital letter) Relating to the varieties of a language or languages spoken chiefly on islands. Insular Latin, Latin as it was spoken in Britain and Ireland. Insular Celtic, the Celtic languages of Britain, Ireland and also Brittany, as opposed to those spoken in mainland Europe other than Brittany. Insular Scandinavian, relating to the Icelandic and Faroese languages as opposed to the ones spoken in Sweden, Denmark and Norway.
Separate or isolated from the surroundings; having little interaction with external parties; provincial.
A polypeptide hormone that regulates carbohydrate metabolism (in various animals including humans).
(uncountable) Action or form of speech deliberately intended to be rude; (countable) a particular act or statement having this effect.
(countable) Something that causes offence (for example, by being of an unacceptable quality).
(transitive) To be insensitive, insolent, or rude to (somebody); to affront or demean (someone). [from 17th c.]
A means of indemnity against a future occurrence of an uncertain event.
The business of providing insurance.
rebellion; revolt; the state of being insurgent
One of several people who take up arms against the local state authority; a participant in insurgency.

(uncountable) The action of part or all of a national population violently rising up against the government or other authority; (countable) an instance of this; a revolt, an uprising; specifically, one that is at an initial stage or limited in nature.
Left complete or whole; not touched, defiled, sullied or otherwise damaged.
Incapable of being perceived by the senses; incorporeal.
(arithmetic) A number that is not a fraction; an element of the infinite and numerable set {..., -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...}.
Constituting a whole together with other parts or factors; not omittable or removable
(mathematics) Of, pertaining to, or being an integer.

(mathematics) One of the two fundamental operations of calculus (the other being differentiation), whereby a function's displacement, area, volume, or other qualities arising from the study of infinitesimal change are quantified, usually defined as a limiting process on a sequence of partial sums. Denoted using a long s: ∫, or a variant thereof.
(enzyme) Any enzyme that integrates viral DNA into that of an infected cell
(semiconductors) A thin chip, usually of silicon, consisting of at least two interconnected semiconductor devices, mainly transistors.
Pertaining to, or performed by, the intellect; mental or cognitive.
An intelligent, learned person, especially one who discourses about learned matters.

(uncountable) Any product of someone's intellect that has commercial value: a piece of literature, a painting, an invention, a trademark, a trade secret, etc. Works protected under intellectual property law, and accorded intellectual property rights such as copyrights and patents.
(mostly, uncountable) The quality of making use or having made use of such capacities: depth of understanding, mental quickness.
(countable) An entity that has such capacities.
(countable) A political or military department, agency or unit designed to gather information, usually secret, about the enemy or about hostile activities.
A governmental agency that is tasked with information gathering (known in the context as "intelligence") for purposes of national security and defense.

A score derived from one of several different standardized tests attempting to measure a person's intelligence relative to that of the general population, with the average usually calibrated to a number around 100.
(politics) The intellectual elite of a society, particularly in Marxist doctrine.
Capable of being understood; clear to the mind.
(ambitransitive, usually followed by particle "to" + verb, or "on"/"upon" + noun) To fix the mind upon (something, or something to be accomplished); be intent upon
Of a characteristic: extreme or very high or strong in degree; severe; also, excessive.
(also, figurative) Under tension; tightly drawn; strained, stressed, tense.
The quality of being intense.
The condition of being intensive.
Something that is intended.
A course of action that a person intends to follow.
Intended or planned; done deliberately or voluntarily.
To bury in a grave.
Interacting with or communicating with and reacting to each other; influencing or having an effect on each other; acting or capable of acting on each other or with the other.
(countable) A junction in which traffic may merge to enter or diverge to exit a limited-access highway to access a surface street, without crossing traffic on the main highway.
(rail transport, countable) A connection between two or more lines, services or modes of transport; a station at which such a connection can be made.
Communication, conversation.
Dealings between countries.
Sexual intercourse usually involving humans.
(transitive, US, military) To impede (an enemy); to interrupt or destroy (enemy communications, supply lines etc). [from 20th c.]

(uncountable, finance) The price paid for obtaining, or price received for providing, money or goods in a credit transaction, calculated as a fraction of the amount or value of what was borrowed. [from earlier 16th c.]
(uncountable) A great attention and concern from someone or something; intellectual curiosity. [from later 18th c.]
(uncountable) Attention that is given to or received from someone or something.
(countable) An involvement, claim, right, share, stake in or link with a financial, business, or other undertaking or endeavor.
(obsolete, often, _, impersonal) To be concerned with or engaged in; to affect; to concern; to excite.
(finance) The percentage of an amount of money charged for its use per some period of time (often a year).
Arousing or holding the attention or interest of someone.
The point of interconnection or contact between entities.
(object-oriented programming) In some languages, a block of code declaring the interface (point of interconnection) between a class and code that interacts with it.
(intransitive) To get involved or involve oneself, causing disturbance.
The act of interfering with something, or something that interferes.
(physics) An effect caused by the superposition of two systems of waves.
A distortion on a broadcast signal due to atmospheric or other effects.
(biochemistry) Any of a group of glycoproteins, produced by the immune system, that prevent viral replication in infected cells.
Occurring between glaciations (colloquially known as ice ages).
The relatively warm period between glacial periods.
Of, relating to, or involving two or more governments.
A transitional or temporary period between other events.

Being between two extremes, or in the middle of a range.
Anything in an intermediate position.
An intermediary.
The act of burying a dead body; burial.

Stopping and starting, occurring, or presenting at intervals; coming after a particular time span.

common to, or affecting, two or more nations.
Of or concerning the association called the International.
Set of rules generally regarded and accepted as binding in relations between states and between nations, serving as a framework for the practice of stable and organized international relations.
(international law) An organisation established by a treaty or other instrument governed by international law and possessing its own international legal personality.

(pharmacology) A particular, minute unit of mass, defined differently for different substances, but so that varying substances of the same general type have the property that one international unit of the one has the same effect on the human body as one international unit of the other.
(dated) A designer, operator, or technically capable professional user of the Internet.
Characterized by struggle within a group, usually applied to an ethnic or familial relationship.
(biology) The stage in the life cycle of a cell between two successive mitotic or meiotic divisions.
To decode the meaning of a topic and then act, whether to continue researching the topic, follow through, act in opposition, or further the understanding through sharing an interpretation.
(countable) An act of interpreting or explaining something unclear; a translation; a version.

A person who converts spoken or signed language into a different language for the benefit of one or more others who do not understand the first language being used (especially if in real time or shortly after that person has finished communicating). (Contrasted with translator.)

(transitive) to question or quiz, especially in a thorough and/or aggressive manner
A question put; an inquiry.

A time interval during which there is a cessation of something.
The junction of two (or more) paths, streets, highways, or other thoroughfares.
(set theory) The set containing all the elements that are common to two or more sets.
(geometry) The point or set of points common to two geometrical objects (such as the point where two lines meet or the line where two planes intersect).

Of, relating to, or situated in an interstice.
(oceanography) The part of a shore between high water and low water, especially the beach exposed at maximum ebb spring tides.
A distance in space.
A period of time.
(intransitive) To occur, fall, or come between, points of time, or events.
The action of intervening; interfering in some course of events.
(medicine) An action taken or procedure performed; an operation.
(anatomy) A disc between the vertebra in the spine.

A conversation in person (or, by extension, over the telephone, Internet etc.) between a journalist and someone whose opinion or statements he or she wishes to record for publication, broadcast etc. [from 19th c.]
Relating to the intestines.
(anatomy, often pluralized) The alimentary canal of an animal through which food passes after having passed all stomachs.
One of certain subdivisions of this part of the alimentary canal, such as the small or large intestine in human beings.
Closely acquainted; familiar.
Personal; private.
To or towards the inside of.
Against, especially with force or violence.
(mathematics) Expressing the operation of division, with the denominator given first. Usually with "goes".
To or towards the region of.
Investigating the subject (of).
(linguistics) The rise and fall of the voice in speaking.
Stupefied by alcohol, drunk.
(grammar) An action verb which does not take a direct object.
Fearless; bold; brave.

Having a great deal of fine detail or complexity.

(transitive) To cause someone to become accustomed to something that requires prolonged or repeated tolerance of one or more unpleasantries. [from 16th c.]
(transitive) To enter by force, usually in order to conquer.

Not variable; unalterable; uniform; always having the same value.

One who invents, either as a hobby or as an occupation.
