(uncountable) A Japanese syllabary used when writing words borrowed from foreign languages other than Chinese, specific names of plants and animals and other jargon, onomatopoeia, or to emphasize a word or phrase. Also used to write the Ainu language.
(weaponry) A type of Japanese longsword, having a single edge and slight curvature, historically used by samurai and ninja.
A relative of grasshoppers and crickets, in the family Tettigoniidae.
A plant from the South Pacific, Piper methysticum.
An intoxicating beverage made from the kava plant.
(chiefly, in the context of Japanese culture, ACG) Cute, adorable.
A type of small boat, covered over by a surface deck, powered by the occupant or occupants using a double-bladed paddle in a sitting position, from a hole in the surface deck
(nautical) A large beam along the underside of a ship’s hull from bow to stern.
(chiefly, Commonwealth) Often with a prepositional phrase, or with to and an infinitive: showing a quick and ardent responsiveness or willingness; eager, enthusiastic, interested.
Having a fine edge or point; sharp.
(historical) The main tower of a castle or fortress, located within the castle walls.
(ditransitive) To maintain the condition of; to preserve in a certain state.
(transitive) To observe; to adhere to; to fulfill; to not swerve from or violate.
(transitive) To restrict or restrain.
(transitive, idiomatic) To continue with (work, etc).
A person charged with guarding or caring for, storing, or maintaining something; a custodian, a guard; sometimes a gamekeeper.

(sports) The player charged with guarding a goal or wicket. Short form of goalkeeper, wicketkeeper. In quidditch (both Muggle quidditch and the game in the original Harry Potter series), this is someone responsible for guarding the three goalposts.
Some object given by a person and retained in memory of something or someone; something kept for sentimental or nostalgic reasons.
A fermented milk drink from the Caucasus and Eastern Europe, similar to yogurt but more liquid.
A round, traditionally wooden container of lesser capacity than a barrel, often used to store beer.
(Internet slang, video games) Used to indicate laughter or humour.
Any of several large brown algae seaweeds (order Laminariales).
(Celtic mythology) A malevolent shapeshifting spirit, most often in the form of a horse, believed to haunt the rivers and lochs of Scotland.
In the International System of Units, the base unit of thermodynamic temperature; 1⁄273.16 of the thermodynamic temperature of the triple point of water. Shown as "K".
(transitive, mostly, Scotland) To know, perceive or understand.
A Japanese martial art using "swords" of split bamboo.
A house or shelter for a dog.
A facility at which dogs are reared or boarded.
(disease) Inflammation of the cornea.
(British, AU, NZ) The raised edge between the pavement and the roadway, typically made of concrete though originally consisting of a line of kerbstones.
(dated) A piece of cloth used to cover the head; a bandana.
(chiefly, Commonwealth, informal) A disorderly outburst, disturbance, commotion, or tumult. [from Template:SAFESUBST: c.]
The core, center, or essence of an object or system.
(botany) The central (usually edible) part of a nut, especially once the hard shell has been removed.
(botany, US) The stone of certain fruits, such as peaches or plums.
(computing) The central part of many computer operating systems which manages the system's resources and the communication between hardware and software components.

(mathematics, linear algebra, group theory, functional analysis) For a given function (especially a linear transformation between vector spaces or homomorphism between groups), the set of elements in the domain which are mapped to zero; (formally) given f : X → Y, the set {x ∈ X : f(x) = 0}.

A thin colorless, blue- or straw-colored petroleum-based fuel heavier than gasoline/petrol or naptha but lighter than diesel, used primarily as jet fuel but also for heating and lighting in some remote or impoverished areas.
Any of various small falcons of the genus Falco that hover while hunting.
(uncountable, chiefly, US, Canada, UK) Ellipsis of tomato ketchup. A tomato-vinegar-based sauce, sometimes containing spices, onion or garlic, and (especially in the US) sweeteners.
(organic compound) A homologous series of organic molecules whose functional group is an oxygen atom joined to a carbon atom—by a double bond—in a carbon-hydrogen based molecule.
(carbohydrate) A saccharide containing a ketone functional group.
A vessel for boiling a liquid or cooking food, usually metal and equipped with a lid.
(musical instruments) A large percussion instrument with a drumhead that is stretched over a hemispherical metal bowl.
Indispensable, supremely important.
Important, salient.
An object designed to open and close a lock.
A crucial step or requirement.
In instruments with a keyboard such as an organ or piano, one of the levers, or especially the exposed front end of it, which are depressed to cause a particular sound or note to be produced.
In musical instruments, one of the valve levers used to select notes, such as a lever opening a hole on a woodwind.
(music) A scale or group of pitches constituting the basis of a musical composition.
(cryptography) A piece of information (e.g., a password or passphrase) used to encode or decode a message or messages.
(databases) In a relational database, a field used as an index into another table (not necessarily unique).
(computing) A value that uniquely identifies an entry in a container.
(biology) A series of logically organized groups of discriminating information which aims to allow the user to correctly identify a taxon.
(music) An indication of the key of a composition, giving the number of sharps or flats in the corresponding scale.
(computing, etc.) A set of keys used to operate a typewriter, computer etc.
(music) A device with keys of a musical keyboard, used to control electronic sound-producing devices which may be built into or separate from the keyboard device.
An ornamental piece holding such a chain or ring.
A single frame in an animation sequence drawn by an artist, between which others are tweened.
(computer graphics) A complete video frame, used as a reference for subsequent interframes in video compression.
Any small opening resembling the hole for a key in shape or function; especially, one that gives a vista of, or access to, a space beyond.
A speech that sets the main theme of a conference or other gathering; a keynote speech or keynote address.
A ring, normally of metal or plastic, for holding keys together.
(architecture) The top stone of an arch.
(historical) A khan of khans, a ruler of a khaganate; (the holder of) an imperial rank used among certain Turkic and Mongolian peoples, equal in status to an emperor.
A dull, yellowish-brown colour, the colour of dust.
(historical) A ruler over various Turkic and Mongol peoples in the Middle Ages.
A shrub, Catha edulis, whose leaves are used as a mild stimulant when chewed or brewed as tea; also a drug produced from this plant.
The title of the hereditary monarch of Egypt from 1805–1914, nominally ruling as a viceroy of the Sultan of Turkey.
a Slavic art form, a combination of a circle dance and chorus singing, similar to chorea of ancient Greece, also in Romania (horă)
Any artificial animal feed in pellet form.
A community, usually an agricultural one in Israel, based on a high level of social and economical sharing, equality, direct democracy and tight social relations.
A person who offers unsolicited views, advice, or criticism; one who kibitzes.
(transitive) To strike or hit with the foot or other extremity of the leg.
(intransitive, UK, idiomatic, colloquial) To be overcome with anger, to start an argument or a fight; to behave aggressively.
(idiomatic, vulgar, chiefly, US, Canada) To clobber someone; to beat someone severely.

A type of small sled consisting of a handlebar mounted on a pair of flexible metal runners. The driver stands on the runners and kicks the sled forward with one foot. In front of the handlebar there's often a seat for a passenger.
(informal) A child (usually), teenager, or young adult; a juvenile.
(colloquial) An inexperienced person or one in a junior position.
(transitive, colloquial) To make a joke with (someone).
(intransitive, colloquial) To joke.
(slang, often, attributive) A child.
(US, Australia, NZ, Philippines) A close friend; especially used as a form of address.
(US, Australia, NZ, Philippines) A child.
The crime, or an instance, of kidnapping.
(crime) The crime of taking a person against their will, sometimes for ransom.
An organ in the body that filters the blood, producing urine.
(medicine) A calculus in the kidney.
A spicy, smoked sausage of a particular kind from Eastern Europe.
(transitive, offensive, uncommon) To render something more Jewish.
(transitive) To put to death; to extinguish the life of.

form.orth: kill two birds with one stone

sense.def: (idiomatic) To solve two problems with one single action.
One who or that which kills.
An oven or furnace or a heated chamber, for the purpose of hardening, burning, calcining or drying anything; for example, firing ceramics, curing or preserving tobacco, or drying grain.
(international standards) Alternative letter-case form of Kilo from the NATO/ICAO Phonetic Alphabet.
(computing, especially, _, networking) One thousand (103, or 1,000) bytes.
A non-SI unit of energy equal to 1,000 calories, used (now rare) in chemistry or physics; equal to 1 calorie as used in nutrition. Symbol kcal.

In the International System of Units, the base unit of mass; conceived of as the mass of one litre of water, but now defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Planck constant h to be 6.626 070 15 × 10-34 when expressed in units of kg⋅m2⋅s−1. Symbol: kg
A unit of frequency equal to one thousand cycles per second; one thousand hertz
A unit of volume equivalent to 1000 litres, and equal to one cubic metre. Symbol: kl
(metrology) An SI unit of length equal to 103 metres. Symbol: km
(chiefly in the negative) Chiefly in out of kilter: (good) condition, form, or order; fettle. [from 17th c.]
A Korean dish made of vegetables, such as cabbage or radishes, that are salted, seasoned, and stored in sealed containers to undergo lactic acid fermentation.
A traditional Japanese T-shaped, wrapped-front garment with square sleeves and a rectangular body, now generally worn only on formal occasions.
One or more relatives, such as siblings or cousins, taken collectively.
Affectionate.
(archaic) One's inherent nature; character, natural disposition.
Goods or services used as payment, as e.g. in barter.
(type theory) The type of a type constructor or a higher-order type operator.
(idiomatic, colloquial) Slightly; somewhat; sort of.
(North America, Australia) An educational institution for young children, usually between ages 4 and 6; nursery school. [from 1852]
(North America, Australia) The elementary school grade before first grade.
(transitive) To start (a fire) or light (a torch, a match, coals, etc.).
Having a kind personality; kind, warmhearted, sympathetic.
Used to make a polite request: please.
(often, plural only) People of the same ethnic descent, not including speaker; brethren.
(idiomatic) Someone with the same feelings or attitudes as oneself.
(US) Relatives, relations.
A male monarch; a man who heads a monarchy; in an absolute monarchy, the supreme ruler of his nation.

(chess) The principal chess piece, that players seek to threaten with unavoidable capture to result in a victory by checkmate. It is often the tallest piece, with a symbolic crown with a cross at the top.
(card games) A playing card with the letter "K" and the image of a king on it, the thirteenth card in a given suit.
A realm having a king and/or queen as its actual or nominal sovereign.
(taxonomy) A rank in the classification of organisms, below domain and above phylum; a taxon at that rank (e.g. the plant kingdom, the animal kingdom).
Fish of genus Caranx
Any of various birds of the suborder Alcedines (or the family Alcedinidae sensu lato), having a large head, short tail and brilliant colouration; they feed mostly on fish.
(chiefly, _, pejorative) A petty king; a king ruling over a small or unimportant territory.
Characteristic of kings, majestic, regal; as befits a king, in the manner of a king.
In a royal manner.
The most important person in an undertaking or organization.
A tight curl, twist, or bend in a length of thin material, hair etc.
Potos flavus, a carnivorous mammal of Central America and South America with a long, prehensile tail, related to the raccoon.
Queer; eccentric; crotchety.
relation or connection by blood, marriage or adoption
relation or connection by nature or character
A male relative.
A small enclosed structure, often freestanding, open on one side or with a window, used as a booth to sell newspapers, cigarettes, etc.
(informal, chiefly, UK) To sleep; often with the connotation of a temporary or charitable situation, or one borne out of necessity.
The cloth skullcap or yarmulke traditionally worn by male Jews.
A knee-length tunic.
Fate; a predetermined or unavoidable destiny.
A touch with the lips, usually to express love or affection, or as a greeting.
(transitive) To touch with the lips or press the lips against, usually to show love or affection or passion, or as part of a greeting.
I informally request that you kiss me—that you touch my lips with your lips or press the lips against, as an expression of love or affection.
(sometimes, vulgar, idiomatic) Go away!; an expression of disdain or dismissal.
Any collection of items needed for a specific purpose, especially for use by a workman, or personal effects packed for travelling.
A room or area for preparing food.
(slang) A public gaming room in a casino.
Any knife used for preparing food.
(UK) Paper towels intended for kitchen purposes such as absorbing spillages and wrapping sandwiches.
(literal) A sink in a kitchen used for washing dishes and preparing food.
A bird of prey of the family Accipitridae.
(geometry) A polygon resembling the shape of a traditional toy kite (sense 3): a quadrilateral having two pairs of edges of equal length, the edges of each pair touching each other at one end.
(sailing, dated) In a square-rigged ship: originally a sail positioned above a topsail; later a lightweight sail set above the topgallants, such as a studding sail or a jib topsail.
(archaic, or, obsolete, uncountable) Friends and acquaintances.
(Northern England, Scotland, rural, countable) An acquaintance or a friend.
Art, decorative objects, and other forms of representation of questionable artistic or aesthetic value; a representation that is excessively sentimental, overdone, or vulgar.
A young cat, especially before sexual maturity (reached at about seven months).
A young rabbit, rat, hedgehog, squirrel, fox, beaver, badger, etc.
Either of two small gulls in the genus Rissa of the family Laridae that nest in colonies on sea cliffs and spend the winter on the open ocean.
(informal) A kitten or young cat, or sometimes adult cat.
A flightless bird of the genus Apteryx native to New Zealand.
A Chinese gooseberry vine fruit, having a hairy brown skin and dark green (or in the case of the kiwi fruit gold, yellow) flesh with fine black seeds, almost always varieties of Actinidia deliciosa.
A loud electric alarm or horn, especially as used in automobiles in the early 20th century. [from 1908]
(historical) An anti-Ottoman insurgent living in the mountains when Greece was a part of the Ottoman Empire.
(psychology) A psychological disorder that causes an uncontrollable obsession with stealing without economic or material need.
(slang, military) A kilometer.
(US, pejorative) A clumsy or stupid person.
A readiness in performance; aptness at doing something. [from 1580]
A petty contrivance; a toy.
(archaic) A boy; especially, a boy servant.
(cards) A playing card marked with the figure of a servant or soldier; a jack.
(transitive) To work and press into a mass, usually with the hands; especially, to work, as by repeated pressure with the knuckles, into a well mixed mass, the materials of bread, cake, etc.
In humans, the joint or the region of the joint in the middle part of the leg between the thigh and the shank.
A protective garment worn on a knee to protect it from injury, for example due to a blow or a fall.
(anatomy) The flat, roundish bone in the knee.
The sound of a bell knelling; a toll (particularly one signalling a death).
(intransitive) To ring a bell slowly, especially for a funeral; to toll.
(transitive) To signal or proclaim something (especially a death) by ringing a bell.

A utensil or a tool designed for cutting, consisting of a flat piece of hard material, usually steel or other metal (the blade), usually sharpened on one edge, attached to a handle. The blade may be pointed for piercing.
A weapon designed with the aforementioned specifications intended for slashing and/or stabbing and too short to be called a sword. A dagger.
Any blade-like part in a tool or a machine designed for cutting, such as that of a chipper.
(by extension) An armored and mounted warrior of the Middle Ages.
(modern) A person on whom a knighthood has been conferred by a monarch.

(chess) A chess piece, often in the shape of a horse's head, that is moved two squares in one direction and one at right angles to that direction in a single move, leaping over any intervening pieces.
A knight in a medieval romance who wanders in search of adventure and opportunities to prove his chivalry.
A long, thin, pointed rod, used in pairs to knit yarn.
A rounded protuberance, especially one arising from a flat surface; a fleshy lump or caruncle.
A rounded control switch that can be turned on its axis, designed to be operated by the fingers.
The head of the penis; the glans.
(cooking) A dollop, an amount just larger than a spoonful (usually referring to butter).
(intransitive) To rap one's knuckles against something, especially wood.
(colloquial, mostly, imperative, idiom) To cease doing something, particularly annoying or unpleasant; to desist.
An imitation of something, particularly a well-known product, usually lower in quality and price than the original.
A small mound or rounded hill.
A looping of a piece of string or of any other long, flexible material that cannot be untangled without passing one or both ends of the material through its loops.
(mathematics) A non-self-intersecting closed curve in (e.g., three-dimensional) space that is an abstraction of a knot (in sense 1 above).

(aviation) A unit of indicated airspeed, calibrated airspeed, or equivalent airspeed, which varies in its relation to the unit of speed so as to compensate for the effects of different ambient atmospheric conditions on aircraft performance.
A leather scourge (multi-tail whip), in the severe version known as 'great knout' with metal weights on each tongue, notoriously used in imperial Russia.
(transitive) To perceive the truth or factuality of; to be certain of; to be certain that.
(intransitive) To have knowledge; to have information, be informed.
(transitive, philosophy) To maintain (a belief, a position) subject to a given philosophical definition of knowledge; to hold a justified true belief.
(transitive) To be acquainted or familiar with; to have encountered.
The knowledge and skill to be able to (do something correctly).
The fact of knowing about something; general understanding or familiarity with a subject, place, situation etc. [from 14th c.]
Any of the joints between the bones of the fingers.
A tree-dwelling marsupial, Phascolarctos cinereus, that resembles a small bear with a broad head, large ears and sharp claws, mainly found in eastern Australia.
Brassica oleracea var. gongylodes, a variety of the cabbage, having a turnip-shaped edible stem.
Ornamental domesticated varieties of the Amur carp (Cyprinus rubrofuscus), of Japan and eastern Asia with red-gold or white coloring.
Any of the kanji characters invented in Japan.
A nut of this tree.
(Christianity) A rope of usually 33, 50 or 100 knots, used in meditative prayer in the Eastern Orthodox and Eastern Catholic tradition, to count one's recitations of the Jesus Prayer.
A kind of long horn instrument from Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
A kapiejka: a Belarusian monetary unit equal to one hundredth of a ruble (rubel).
The currency of the Czech Republic, divided into 100 hellers.
The former currency of Slovakia, divided into 100 haliers.
A fermented drink made from mare's milk, common among peoples of the Central Asian steppes.
The act of kowtowing.
(intransitive, figuratively) To grovel, act in a very submissive manner.
Strong paper made from kraft pulp, often used for making corrugated board.
(administrative division) A region or province in Russia.
(historical) A small coin of varying value formerly used in parts of Germany and Austria.
The official currency of Sweden.
The currency of Iceland, Denmark (including Greenland and the Faroe Islands) and Norway, divided into 100 øre, except in Iceland where 1 króna = 100 aurar.
The chemical element (symbol Kr) with an atomic number of 36. It is a colourless, odourless noble gas that only reacts with fluorine. It is one of the rarest gases in the Earth's atmosphere.
The currency of Iceland, divided into 100 aurar
Praise; accolades.
Credit for one's achievements.
A traditional savoury or sweet Jewish dish consisting of a baked pudding of pasta, potatoes, or rice, with vegetables, or raisins and spices.
A small, orange citrus-like fruit which is native to Asia (Citrus japonica, syn. Fortunella japonica).
(martial arts) The Chinese martial arts collectively.
(chemistry, physics) A rejected name for rutherfordium.
A fermented cereal-based low alcoholic beverage, often flavored with fruit, honey and herbs.
A person who endlessly whines or complains; a person who finds fault with anything.
To whine or complain, often needlessly and incessantly.
A Japanese form of archery.
The traditional form of Japanese kanji used before 1947.
(music) A syllable used in solfège to represent the sixth note of a major scale.
(idiomatic) A person or group used as the subject of an experiment or test, especially unwillingly or unwittingly.
A small ticket or sign giving information about something to which it is attached or intended to be attached.
(transitive) To put a label (a ticket or sign) on (something).
(anatomy, zootomy) Of or pertaining to the lips or labia.
Liable to slip, err, fall, or apostatize.
(phonetics) A speech sound articulated with the lower lip and upper teeth.
(anatomy, usually, in the plural) A liplike structure; especially one of the vulva's two pairs of folds of skin on either side.
A room, building or institution equipped for scientific research, experimentation or analysis.
A place where chemicals, drugs or microbes are prepared or manufactured.
One who uses bodily strength rather than intellect to earn a wage, usually hourly.
Requiring much physical effort; toilsome.
That which requires hard work for its accomplishment; that which demands effort.
(uncountable) Workers in general; the working class, the workforce; sometimes specifically the labour movement, organised labour.
(medicine, obstetrics) The act of a mother giving birth.
The time period during which a mother gives birth.
(intransitive) To toil, to work.
(by extension) Anything complicated and confusing in structure, arrangement, or character.
(gardening) A maze formed by paths separated by high hedges.

(anatomy) A complex structure in the inner ear which contains the organs of hearing and balance. It consists of bony cavities (the bony labyrinth) filled with fluid and lined with sensitive membranes (the membranous labyrinth).
A type of mechanical seal that provides a tortuous path to help prevent leakage.
Physically resembling a labyrinth; with the qualities of a maze.
(pathology) Inflammation of the labyrinth of the inner ear.
A resinous substance or lacquer produced mainly on the banyan tree by the female of Kerria lacca, a scale insect.
(uncountable) A light fabric containing patterns of holes, usually built up from a single thread. Wp
(transitive) To add alcohol, poison, a drug or anything else potentially harmful to (food or drink).
A deficiency or need (of something desirable or necessary); an absence, want.
(transitive, stative) To be without, not to have, to need, to require.
Showing no interest, vigor, determination, or enthusiasm.
Lazy; slothful; indolent.
A footman, a liveried male servant.
A fawning, servile follower.
Foolish; idiotic or simple-minded.
Using as few words as possible; pithy and concise.
A glossy, resinous material used as a surface coating; either a natural exudation of certain trees, or a solution of nitrocellulose in alcohol, etc.
(anatomy) Of or relating to tears or the tear-secreting organs.

cit.quote: 長曲棍球 长曲棍球

sense.def: (sports) A sport played on a field between two opposing teams using sticks (crosses) and a ball, whereby one team defeats the other by scoring more goals within the allotted time.
(enzyme, organic compound) A β-galactosidase enzyme that is involved in the hydrolysis of the disaccharide lactose into constituent galactose and glucose monomers.
Of, relating to, or derived from milk.
(carboxylic acid) 2-hydroxy-propanoic acid (CH3.CHOH.CO2H), a syrupy liquid, soluble in water; found in milk, wine and many fruits; used as a food additive and in many industrial applications.
(carbohydrate) The disaccharide sugar of milk and dairy products, C12H22O11, a product of glucose and galactose used as a food and in medicinal compounds.
A boy or young man.
A familiar term of address for a young man.
A frame, usually portable, of wood, metal, or rope, used for ascent and descent, consisting of two side pieces to which are fastened rungs (cross strips or rounds acting as steps).
In the game of go, a sequence of moves following a zigzag pattern and ultimately leading to the capture of the attacked stones.
(chiefly, Britain) A length of unravelled fabric in a knitted garment, especially in nylon stockings; a run.
Heavy.
(informal) A young woman who behaves in a laddish manner, namely being boisterous and loud and drinking to excess.
A deep-bowled spoonlike utensil with a long, usually curved, handle.
A woman of breeding or higher class, a woman of authority.
A title for someone married to a lord or gentleman.
A woman to whom the particular homage of a knight was paid; a woman to whom one is devoted or bound.
(polite, or, used by children) A woman: an adult female human.
Any of the Coccinellidae family of beetles, typically having a round shape and red or yellow spotted elytra.
Term of respect for a woman of the peerage without using her title.
(chiefly, Louisiana, Mississippi, Trinidad and Tobago) An extra or unexpected gift or benefit, such as that given to customers when they purchase something.
A place inhabited by a wild animal, often a cave or a hole in the ground.
A shed or shelter for domestic animals.
(economics, politics) A policy of governmental non-interference in economic affairs.
(now, _, chiefly, _, dialectal) A small stream of running water; a channel for water; a drain.
A master of Tibetan Buddhism.
A young sheep.
(uncountable) The flesh of a lamb or sheep used as food.
(figuratively) A person who is meek, docile and easily led.
(preceded by definite article) A fast-paced, erotic Brazilian dance in which couples dance with their stomachs touching.
To scold, reprimand or criticize harshly.
Unable to walk properly because of a problem with one's feet or legs.
(colloquial) Unconvincing or unbelievable.
(colloquial) Synonym of uncool, uninteresting, or unfunny.
An expression of grief, suffering, sadness or regret.
A song expressing grief.
(intransitive) To express grief; to weep or wail; to mourn.
(transitive) To express great sorrow or regret over; to bewail.
Thin wire or foil made of brass, gold or silver; now especially thin strips of metallic foil used as Christmas decoration.
A thin layer, plate, or scale of material.
A device that generates heat, light or other radiation. Especially an electric light bulb.
A device containing oil, burnt through a wick for illumination; an oil lamp.
A small oil lamp.
The pole that holds up a light so it can illuminate a wide area, such as holds up a streetlight.
Any long slender primitive eel-like freshwater and saltwater fish of the order Petromyzontiformes, having a sucking mouth with rasping teeth but no jaw.
A cover over a lamp to either diffuse the light or to block it in certain directions to avoid glare in the eyes.
A weapon of war, consisting of a long shaft or handle and a steel blade or head; a spear carried by horsemen.
A wooden spear, sometimes hollow, used in jousting or tilting, designed to shatter on impact with the opposing knight’s armour.
(fishing) A spear or harpoon used by whalers and fishermen.
(military) A soldier armed with a lance; a lancer.
A sharp, pointed, two-edged surgical instrument used in venesection and for opening abscesses etc.
The part of Earth which is not covered by oceans or other bodies of water.
Real estate or landed property; a partitioned and measurable area which is owned and acquired and on which buildings and structures can be built and erected.
(agriculture) The ground left unploughed between furrows; any of several portions into which a field is divided for ploughing.
A country or region.
A person's country of origin and/or homeplace; homeland.
(intransitive) To descend to a surface, especially from the air.
(transitive) To bring to land.
(transitive) To acquire; to secure.
A spacecraft, particularly a probe, designed to set down on the surface of another celestial body.
An arrival at a surface, as of an airplane or any descending object.
A place on a shoreline where a boat lands.
A female landlord.
(by extension) A telephone connected by such a fixed wire, specifically not wireless/mobile.
(of a country, geographical region, etc.) Surrounded by land (having no borders with the sea).
A person that leases real property; a lessor.
(surfing, slang, with "the") A shark, imagined as the owner of the surf to be avoided.
(chiefly, British) The owner or manager of a public house.
A recognizable natural or man-made feature used for navigation.
(figurative, also, attributive) A major event or discovery.
A portion of land or territory which the eye can comprehend in a single view, including all the objects it contains.
A picture representing a real or imaginary scene by land or sea, the main subject being the general aspect of nature, as fields, hills, forests, water, etc.
The pictorial aspect of a country.
A space, indoor or outdoor and natural or man-made (as in "designed landscape")
A natural disaster that involves the breakup and downhill flow of rock, mud, water and anything caught in the path.
The sliding of a mass of land down a cliff or slope; a landslide.
A lengthwise division of roadway intended for a single line of vehicles.
(athletics) A similar division of a racetrack to keep runners apart.
A course designated for ships or aircraft.
(countable) A body of words, and set of methods of combining them (called a grammar), understood by a community and used as a form of communication.
(uncountable) The ability to communicate using words.
(uncountable) A sublanguage: the slang of a particular community or jargon of a particular specialist field.
(countable, uncountable, figurative) The expression of thought (the communication of meaning) in a specified way; that which communicates something, as language does.

To perceive; to come to a knowledge of; to have personal acquaintance with; to experience; to suffer.
(transitive, colloquial) To meet (a person) by arrangement.
A gathering of persons for a purpose; an assembly.
(collective) The people at such a gathering.
(geometry) A polygon with one million sides.
A large stone slab making up a prehistoric monument, or part of such a monument.
A prehistoric monument made up of one or more large stones.
A psychopathological condition characterized by delusional fantasies of wealth, power, or omnipotence.
A large conurbation, where two or more large cities have sprawled outward to meet, forming something larger than a metropolis; a megacity.
A distance of 1,000 km. Symbol: Mm
A portable, usually hand-held, funnel-shaped device that is used to amplify a person’s natural voice toward a targeted direction.
One million (1 000 000) watts, abbreviated as MW.
A type of flatfish of the genus Lepidorhombus native to the northeastern Atlantic Ocean; specifically, the Cornish sole, sail-fluke, witch or whiff (Lepidorhombus whiffiagonis).
(usually, uncountable, cytology) Cell division of a diploid cell into four haploid cells, which develop to produce gametes.
A transuranic chemical element (symbol Mt) with atomic number 109.
Filled with or affected by melancholy—great sadness or depression, especially of a thoughtful or introspective nature.
Great sadness or depression, especially of a thoughtful or introspective nature.
(biochemistry) Any of a group of naturally occurring dark pigments, especially the pigment found in skin, hair, fur, and feathers.
(oncology, disease) A dark-pigmented, usually malignant tumor arising from a melanocyte and occurring most commonly in the skin.
Any material similar in its chemistry and effect to the natural hormone.
Lively contention or debate, skirmish.
Melodious, tuneful.
A free-reed keyboard wind instrument.
Having a pleasant melody or sound; tuneful.
In a melodious manner.
A sequence of notes that makes up a musical phrase
One with an abnormal fondness of music; a person who loves music. [from 19th c.]
(uncountable) The large, round to ovoid fruits that have rinds and are of such plants
(ergative) To change (or to be changed) from a solid state to a liquid state, usually by a gradual heat.
(intransitive, figuratively) To dissolve, disperse, vanish.

(transitive, figurative) To soften, as by a warming or kindly influence; to relax; to render gentle or susceptible to mild influences; sometimes, in a bad sense, to take away the firmness of; to weaken.
The process of changing the state of a substance from solid to liquid by heating it past its melting point.
(chemistry, physics) The temperature at which the solid and liquid phases of a substance are in equilibrium; it is relatively insensitive to changes in pressure.
(figurative) A place where many divergent things (often races or cultures, but also talents) come together and are homogenized.
One who belongs to a group.
Part of an animal capable of performing a distinct office; an organ; a limb.
(euphemism) The penis.
The body of members of an organization.
(math) The fact of being a member of a set.
(anatomy, zootomy) A flexible enclosing or separating tissue forming a plane or film and separating two environments.
A mechanical, thin, flat flexible part that can deform or vibrate when excited by an external force.
A piece of parchment forming part of a roll.
A keepsake; an object kept as a reminder of a place or event.
A short note; a memorandum.
A biography; a book describing the experiences of a subject from personal knowledge of the subject or from sources with personal knowledge of the subject.
A short note serving as a reminder.
To fully learn so as to have entirely available to the memory; to learn by heart, commit to memory.
(uncountable) The ability of the brain to record information or impressions with the facility of recalling them later at will.
(computing) The part of a computer that stores variable executable code or data (RAM) or unalterable executable code or default data (ROM).
(computing) Any of several faults in the memory allocation logic of a computer or program whereby parts of memory become hidden or unusable.
(collective, dated) (The) people, humanity, man(kind).
A perceived threat or danger. [a. 1300]
(of a person) Lying, untruthful or dishonest.
(countable) A deceit, falsehood, or lie.
(chemistry) A transuranic chemical element (symbol Md, formerly Mv) with atomic number 101.
Depending on alms for a living.
A pauper who lives by begging.
Male people in general.
The male members of a group.
A servant, especially a domestic servant.
The final menstrual period of a woman after which ovulation no longer occurs.
A pad of absorbent material (such as cotton) used to absorb menstrual flow.
The periodic discharging of the menses, the flow of blood and cells from the lining of the uterus in unfertilized females of humans and other primates.
(lutherie) The measurement of the length of the vibrating string from the nut to the bridge.
(relational) Of or relating to the mind or specifically the total emotional and intellectual response of an individual to external reality.
Arithmetical calculations using only the human brain, with no help from any supplies (such as pencil and paper) or devices such as a calculator.
(uncountable, psychiatry) The property of being mentally ill; mental disorders taken as a whole.
(countable, psychiatry) A mental disorder.
A mindset; a way of thinking; a set of beliefs.

(organic compound) A cyclic monoterpene alcohol; the major component of the essential oil of peppermint; used in pharmaceutical preparations as an antitussive and antipruritic agent, as a nasal decongestant, and in menthol cigarettes.
To make a short reference to something.
A wise and trusted counselor or teacher.
The details of the food to be served at a banquet; a bill of fare.

A list containing the food and beverages served at a restaurant, café, or bar. Menus may be printed on paper sheets provided to customers, put on a large poster or display board inside the establishment, displayed outside the restaurant, or digital.
(computing, gaming) A list from which the user may select an operation to be performed, often done with a keyboard, mouse, or controller under a graphical user interface
The cry of a cat.
(countable) The cry of a cat.
The act of uttering a meow.
(historical, economics) The theory that a nation must always have a positive balance of trade, in the manner that a merchant would operate a shop. Typically this model presupposes protectionism.
Motivated by private gain.
A person employed to fight in an armed conflict who is not a member of the state or military group for which they are fighting and whose primary motivation is private gain.
(uncountable) Goods which are or were offered or intended for sale.
A person who traffics in commodities for profit.
Showing mercy.
(science, historical) One of the elemental principles formerly thought to be present in all metals. [from 15th c.]
(uncountable) Forgiveness or compassion, especially toward those less fortunate.
Just, only; no more than, pure and simple, neither more nor better than might be expected. [from 16th c.]
(focus) Without any other reason etc.; only, just, and nothing more. [from 16th c.]
(transitive, intransitive) To combine into a whole.
The act or process of merging two or more parts into a single unit.
(economics) The legal union of two or more corporations into a single entity, typically assets and liabilities being assumed by the buying party.
(legal) An absorption of one or more estate(s) or contract(s) into one other, all being held by the same owner; of several counts of accusation into one judgement, etc.

(also, geography) In full terrestrial meridian: a great circle on the Earth's surface, passing through the geographic poles (the terrestrial North Pole and South Pole); also, half of such a circle extending from pole to pole, all points of which have the same longitude. [from 14th c.]
A mixture consisting of beaten egg whites and sugar which is added to the tops of pies then browned.
A shell made of this mixture which serves as the receptacle for fruit, ice cream or sherbet.
(countable) A claim to commendation or a reward.
(countable, uncountable) Something deserving or worthy of positive recognition or reward.
(transitive) To deserve, to earn.
(intransitive) To be deserving or worthy.
A mythological creature with a woman's head and upper body, and a tail of a fish.
A legendary creature, human male from the waist up, fishlike from the waist down.
(semantics) A term used to denote a thing that is a part of something else.
A mythological creature with a human upper half (head, arms, and torso) and a piscine lower half.
A state of enjoyable exuberance.
Jolly and full of high spirits; happy.
(Australia, New Zealand, Philippines, Canada, US) Used to express good wishes on or before Christmas Day.

A carousel; a pleasure ride, typically found at fairs and amusement parks, consisting of a slowly revolving circular platform on which various seats are fixed, frequently shaped like horses or other animals.
A piece of playground equipment consisting of a circular platform that is made to revolve by pushing while users stand on it.
A structure made of connected strands of metal, fiber, or other flexible/ductile material, with evenly spaced openings between them.

(embryology) One of the three tissue layers in the embryo of a metazoan animal. Through embryonic development, it will produce many internal organs of the adult, e.g. muscles, spine and circulatory system.
(now specifically, particle) An elementary particle that is composed of a quark and an antiquark, such as a kaon or pion. (Mesons composed of rarer quarks are much heavier.)
(meteorology) The layer of the Earth's atmosphere that is directly above the stratosphere and directly below the thermosphere.
A disagreeable mixture or confusion of things; hence, a situation resulting from blundering or from misunderstanding.
(slang) To diss; to put down.
A communication, or what is communicated; any concept or information conveyed.
An underlying theme or conclusion to be drawn from something.
To send a message to; to transmit a message to, e.g. as text via a cell phone.
One who brings messages.
(Abrahamic tradition) The one who is ordained by God to lead the people of Israel, believed by Christians and Muslims to be Jesus Christ.
Transcending, encompassing.

Pertaining to a level above or beyond; reflexive or recursive; about itself or about other things of the same type. For example, metadata is data that describes data, metalanguage is language that describes language, etc. [From 17th century]
Having analogies with metaphysics.
(physiology) The chemical processes that occur within a living organism in order to maintain life.
Any substance produced by, or taking part in, a metabolic reaction.
Any of a number of chemical elements in the periodic table that form a metallic bond with other metal atoms; generally shiny, somewhat malleable and hard, often a conductor of heat and electricity.
A hand-held device that uses electromagnetic induction to detect buried metal.
A structure, similar to a doorway, through which people pass; an alarm is sounded if the person is carrying a metal object, as this may indicate a weapon.
(linguistics, translation studies, critical theory) Any language or vocabulary of specialized terms used to describe or analyze a language or linguistic process
(computing) Any similar language used to define a programming language
Of, relating to, or characteristic of metal.
(of a color) Having the appearance of being of polished metal.
(chemistry) An element, such as silicon or germanium, intermediate in properties between that of a metal and a nonmetal; especially an elemental semiconductor.
The science of metals; their extraction from ores, purification and alloying, heat treatment, and working.

(geology) one of the major groups of rock that makes up the crust of the Earth; consists of pre-existing rock mass in which new minerals or textures are formed at higher temperatures and greater pressures than those present on the Earth's surface
A transformation, such as one performed by magic.
A noticeable change in character, appearance, function or condition.
(pathology) A change, usually degenerative, in the structure of a specific body tissue.

(uncountable, figure of speech) The use of a word or phrase to refer to something other than its literal meaning, invoking an implicit similarity between the thing described and what is denoted by the word or phrase.
(countable, figure of speech) A word or phrase used in such implied comparison.
Pertaining to or characterized by a metaphor; figurative; symbolic.
Of or pertaining to metaphysics.
branch of philosophy that studies first principles

(medicine) The transference of a bodily function or disease to another part of the body, specifically the development of a secondary area of disease remote from the original site, as with some cancers.
(phonetics, prosody) The transposition of letters, syllables or sounds within a word, such as in ask as /æks/.
To distribute something in portions; to apportion or dole out.
A fast-moving streak of light in the night sky caused by the entry of extraterrestrial matter into the earth's atmosphere; a shooting star or falling star. [from 16th c.]
A metallic or stony object or body that is the remains of a meteoroid.
Of or pertaining to meteorology.
The science that deals with the study of the atmosphere and its phenomena, especially with weather and weather forecasting.
A device that measures things.
A highly addictive phenethylamine stimulant drug. Its systematic (IUPAC) name is (S)-N-methyl-1-phenylpropan-2-amine.
(organic compound, uncountable) The simplest aliphatic hydrocarbon, CH₄, being a constituent of natural gas, and one of the most abundant greenhouse gases.

(organic compound) The simplest aliphatic alcohol, CH3OH; a colourless, toxic, inflammable liquid, used as a solvent, antifreeze, in the chemical industry, and in the preparation of methylated spirit.
(countable) A process by which a task is completed; a way of doing something (followed by the adposition of, to or for before the purpose of the process).
(object-oriented) A subroutine or function belonging to a class or object.
In an organized manner; proceeding with regard to method; systematic.
(originally, sciences) The study of methods used in a field.
(loosely) A collection of methods, practices, procedures and rules used by those who work in some field.
The implementation of such methods etc.
(genetics) The addition of a methyl group to cytosine and adenine residues in DNA that leads to the epigenetic modification of DNA and the reduction of gene expression and protein production.
Characterized by very precise, conscientious attention to details.
In a meticulous manner.

The basic unit of length in the International System of Units (SI: Système International d'Unités), equal to the distance travelled by light in a vacuum in 1/299 792 458 seconds. The metre is equal to 39+47⁄127 (approximately 39.37) imperial inches.
An SI derived unit for measuring speed or velocity.
(chiefly, _, US) A unit of mass equal to 1000 kilograms, about 2204.6 pounds avoirdupois.
(prosody) The basic unit of the underlying rhythm of verse.
(rail, British spelling) The process of converting a railway to a metro-style service.
(uncountable) The science of weights and measures or of measurement.
(music) A device, containing an inverted pendulum, used to mark time by means of regular ticks at adjustable intervals; an electronic equivalent that emits flashes.
(history, especially, Ancient Greece) The mother (founding) polis (city state) of a colony.
A large, busy city, especially as the main city in an area or country or as distinguished from surrounding rural areas.
A quality of courage and endurance.
Marked by mettle or bravery; courageous.
(archaic, poetic, dialectal) A gull, seagull.
(Canada, US) The lowest balcony in an auditorium, cinema, theatre, etc.; the dress circle.
(music) A syllable used in sol-fa (solfège) to represent the third note of a major scale.
(biology) The branch of biology that deals with microorganisms, especially their effects on man and other living organisms.
integrated circuit
(computing, electronics) A microcomputer on a single chip, used to control some device such as an automobile engine or a toy.
(astronomy) A stellar outburst about one millionth the strength of a classical nova.
(microbiology) An organism that is too small to be seen by the unaided eye; especially, a single-celled organism, such as a bacterium.
A device (transducer) used to convert sound waves into a varying electric current; normally fed into an amplifier and either recorded or transmitted over radio.
(computer hardware) The entire CPU of a computer on a single integrated circuit (chip).
An optical instrument used for observing small objects.
Of, or relating to microscopes or microscopy; microscopal
So small that it can only be seen with the aid of a microscope.
Very small; minute
An electromagnetic wave with wavelength between that of infrared light and radio waves.
An oven that uses microwave energy to heat food or other items placed within it.
Amid.
The middle of the air, as while in flight.
Located in the middle; in between.
Central.
A centre, midpoint.
The part between the beginning and the end.
The central part of a human body; the waist.
That period of life directly preceding old age, often defined roughly as ages 45–65; midlife.
(anatomy) The cavity in the temporal bone between the eardrum and the inner ear that contains the ossicles, and which conveys sound to the cochlea.
The finger between the forefinger and the ring finger.
(idiomatic) A compromise position between extremes.
The characteristic parts of a perfume that emerge only after a waiting period.
(schools, countable) A school which crosses the traditional divide between primary school and secondary school.
An intermediate dealer between the manufacturer and the retailer or customer.
(sports) A player who operates behind the attackers and in front of the defence.

any of various small two-winged flies, for example, from the family Chironomidae or non-biting midges, the family Chaoboridae or phantom midges, and the family Ceratopogonidae or biting midges, all belonging to the order Diptera
(sometimes, offensive) A normally-proportioned person with small stature, usually defined as reaching an adult height less than 4'10". [from later 19th c.]
(sometimes, offensive) Any short person.
Twelve o'clock at night exactly.
(anatomy) The middle section of the human torso, from below the chest to above the waist; the abdomen and its back part.
(often, literary) A place in the middle of something; may be used of a literal or metaphorical location.
That happens in the middle of the week.
A person, usually a woman, who is trained to assist women in childbirth, but who is not a physician.
(transitive) To act as a midwife.
The winter solstice; about December 21st or 22nd.
(countable, uncountable) Demeanor; facial expression or attitude, especially one which is intended by its bearer.
(countable) A specific facial expression.
A small argument; a quarrel.
(intransitive) To become slightly offended.
(countable, uncountable) Power, strength, force or influence held by a person or group.
(uncountable) The ability to do something.
(uncountable) Physical strength or force.
(auxiliary) Used to indicate conditional or possible actions.
Very strong; possessing might.
(pathology) A severe, disabling headache, usually affecting only one side of the head, and often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, photophobia and visual disturbances.
(of birds, etc) Migrating.
(history) A former title of the emperors of Japan during a certain period.
(informal) A microphone.
(dated, of a mammal) Currently producing milk for its offspring.
Gentle and not easily angered.
(of an illness or pain) Not serious or dangerous.
(of weather) Moderately warm, especially less cold than expected.
(plant disease) A growth of minute powdery or webby fungi, whitish or of different colors, found on various diseased or decaying substances.
Any of several customary units of length derived from the 1593 English statute mile of 8 furlongs, equivalent to 5,280 feet or 1,760 yards of various precise values.
Any of many customary units of length from other measurement systems of roughly similar values, as the Chinese mile or Arabic mile.
(slang) One mile per hour, as a measure of speed.
A stone milepost (or by extension in other materials), one of a series of numbered markers placed along a road at regular intervals, typically at the side of the road or in a median.
(idiomatic) An important event in a person's life or career, in the history of a nation, in the life of some project, etc.
(specifically) A social environment or setting.
An ideology which claims that the military is the foundation of a society's security, and thereby its most important aspect.
Characteristic of members of the armed forces.
(North America) Relating to armed forces such as the army, marines, navy and air force (often as distinguished from civilians or police forces).
Relating to war.
Relating to armies or ground forces.
Armed forces.
(military) A show of troops, an assembly of troops as a show of force, to receive orders, or especially for inspection at set times.
The armed forces of a nation together with the industries that supply their weapons and materiel.
(uncountable, by extension) A white (or whitish) liquid obtained from a vegetable source such as almonds, coconuts, oats, rice, and/or soy beans.
(countable, informal) An individual serving of milk.
A male milk sibling.
Pulverized milk solids, produced by evaporating all liquid from milk.
Any tooth of the first set of teeth of young people (or animals).
An animal, such as a dairy cow, kept for the milk it produces.
A thick beverage consisting of milk and ice cream mixed together, often with fruit, chocolate, or other flavoring.
(New England, Australia, New Zealand) A thin beverage, similar to the above, but with no ice cream or significantly less of it.
(mechanics, informal) Accidental emulsion of oil and water in an engine.
(by extension, pejorative) An easily frightened, ineffectual, or weak person.
Resembling milk in color, consistency, smell, etc.; consisting of milk.
The building housing such a grinding apparatus.
A manufacturing plant for paper, steel, textiles, etc.
A building housing such a plant.
(transitive) To grind or otherwise process in a mill or other machine.
Thousand-year-old; also (by extension, loosely) thousands of years old.
Occurring every thousand years.
Referring to the thousandth anniversary of an event or happening.

(by extension, originally, US, demography) Often capitalized: of or relating to, or characteristic of, people born in the last two decades of the 20th century from around the early 1980s to the mid 1990s (with 1996 births cited as the last Millennial year), and who reached adulthood early in the third millennium C.E.

(Christianity) Synonym of millenarian (“pertaining to the belief in an impending period of one thousand years of peace and righteousness associated with the Second Coming of Christ and his reign on earth”)
(with definite article) The year in which one period of one thousand years ends and another begins, especially the year 2000.
A person who owns or operates a mill, especially a flourmill.
Any of a group of various types of grass or its grains used as food, widely cultivated in the developing world.
(metrology) An SI unit of mass equal to 10−3 grams. Symbol: mg
(British spelling) A unit of measure of capacity, being one thousandth of a litre. Symbol: ml
An SI/MKS unit of measure, the length of 1⁄1000 of a metre. Symbol: mm
(mechanical engineering) A rotary cutting tool typically used in milling machines.
(long and short scales) The cardinal number 1,000,000: 106; a thousand thousand.
A person whose net worth is at or greater than one million units of the local currency.
A million times so
(metrology) An SI unit of time equal to 10−3 seconds. Symbol: ms; one one-thousandth of a second. Symbol: ms.
One thousandth (10-3) of a watt, abbreviated as mW.
A large round stone used for grinding grain.
The semen of a male fish.
To make mimeograph copies.
To imitate, especially in order to ridicule.
(biology) To take on the appearance of another, for protection or camouflage.
An act or ability to simulate or effect the appearance of someone or something else.
(historical) A monetary unit of ancient Greece and the Middle East, originally equivalent to the weight of a mina of silver. [From 15th C.]
The capability for rational thought.
The ability to be aware of things.
The ability to remember things.
The ability to focus the thoughts.
Judgment, opinion, or view.
Desire, inclination, or intention.
A way of thinking; an attitude or opinion, especially a habitual one.
An excavation from which ore or solid minerals are taken, especially one consisting of underground tunnels.
A person who works in a mine.
of, related to, or containing minerals
(geology) Any naturally occurring material that has a (more or less) definite chemical composition and characteristic physical properties; especially, an inorganic one.
Any inorganic material (as distinguished from animal or vegetable).
(nutrition) Any inorganic element that is essential to nutrition; a dietary mineral.
water from a spring that naturally contains dissolved minerals, often treated in any of several ways (filtering, aerating etc) and bottled; used either therapeutically or out of preference
(petrology) The branch of petrology that studies minerals.
A vertical hole through the strata to reach the mineral which is being mined.
A vehicle, device or person with the purpose of removing explosive mines (landmines or water mines).
(uncountable, computing, video games) A logic-based computer game in which the player has to discover the position of mines in a rectangular grid, based on numerical hints.
One who works in a mine.
(transitive) To intermix; to combine or join, as an individual or part, with other parts, but commonly so as to be distinguishable in the product.
A small bus, especially one used as transport for small groups.
(music) A half note, drawn as a semibreve with a stem.
The smallest possible amount, quantity, or degree.
(phonology) A pair of words differing by only one phonetic segment or suprasegment, used to prove the validity of a proposed phoneme, toneme, or chroneme.
To the lowest degree.
The lowest limit.
The activity of removing solid valuables from the earth.
A sycophantic follower.
(uncountable, US, _, printing, typography, dated) A size of type between nonpareil and minion, standardized as 6½-point.
(government) A politician who heads a ministry

Government department, at the administrative level normally headed by a minister (or equivalent rank, e.g. secretary of state), who holds it as portfolio, especially in a constitutional monarchy, but also as a polity
The complete body of government ministers (whether or not they are in cabinet) under the leadership of a head of government (such as a prime minister)
A light gray or white fur used to trim the robes of judges or state executives, also used in medieval times.
(music) Incorporating a minor third interval above the (in scales) tonic or (in chords) root note, (also, _, figurative) tending to produce a dark, discordant, sad, or pensive effect.
Lesser, smaller in importance, size, degree, seriousness, or significance compared to another option, particularly:
(Scots law, obsolete) An adolescent, a person above the legal age of puberty but below the age of majority.
(music) A musical key based upon a minor scale.
(astronomy) An astronomical object in direct orbit around the Sun that is not a planet or a comet.
(music) A musical interval in Western music that approximates a frequency ratio of 6:5, spanning two degrees of the diatonic scale.

(historical) Originally, an entertainer employed to juggle, play music, sing, tell stories, etc.; a buffoon, a fool, a jester; later, a medieval (especially travelling) entertainer who would recite and sing poetry, often to their own musical accompaniment.
A building or institution where money (originally, only coins) is produced under government licence.
The flavouring of the plant, either a sweet, a jelly or sauce.
To invent; to forge; to fabricate; to fashion.
(arithmetic) A number or quantity from which another is to be subtracted.
A slow graceful dance consisting of a coupé, a high step, and a balance.
(music) A complete short musical composition inspired by and conforming to many formal characteristics of the traditional musical accompaniment to the dance of same name.
Being a negative quantity; pertaining to a deficit or reduction. [from 18th c.]
That is below zero by (a specified amount) on a scale. [from 19th c.]
(postpositive) Ranking just below (a designated rating). [from 19th c.]
(mathematics) A negative quantity. [from 18th c.]
(mathematics) Made less or reduced by (followed by an expression of number or quantity). [from 15th c.]
(arithmetic) The symbol −, used to denote the operation of subtraction or to indicate that a number is negative.
A unit of time which is one sixtieth of an hour (sixty seconds).
(informal) A short but unspecified time period.
A unit of angle equal to one-sixtieth of a degree.
A unit of purchase on a telephone or other similar network, especially a cell phone network, roughly equivalent in gross form to sixty seconds' use of the network.
An angle, one sixtieth (1/60th) of a degree, used by gunners as a measurement of accuracy. One minute of angle is roughly equal to 1 inch at 100 yards distance.
The official notes kept during a meeting.
An event that appears inexplicable by the laws of nature and so is held to be supernatural in origin.
A fortunate outcome that prevails despite overwhelming odds against it.
An awesome and exceptional example of something
By supernatural or uncommon causes, e.g. by a god; that cannot be explained in terms of normal events.
An optical phenomenon in which light is refracted through a layer of hot air close to the ground, often giving the illusion of a body of water.
A smooth surface, usually made of glass with reflective material painted on the underside, that reflects light so as to give an image of what is in front of it.
(transitive) Of an event, activity, behaviour, etc, to be identical to; to be a copy of.
That which causes merriment.
Hatred of, contempt for, or prejudice against men.
One who has a negative view of the entire human race. This may express itself as, e.g., distrust, dislike, hate, or contempt.
(law) An error at a trial which led to an unjust outcome, such as the conviction of a person for a crime they did not commit.
To have a miscarriage; to involuntarily abort a foetus. [from 16th c.]
To fail to achieve some purpose; to be unsuccessful, to go wrong (of a business, project etc.). [from 16th c.]
Consisting of a variety of ingredients or parts.
(countable) An assortment of miscellaneous items.
(countable) A collection of writings on various subjects or topics; an anthology.
(uncountable) Harm or trouble caused by an agent or brought about by a particular cause.
Causing mischief; injurious.
Troublesome, cheeky, badly behaved.
One not restrained by moral principles; an unscrupulous villain.
That which was done that should not have been, ranging from any sin or moral offense to various degrees of crime.
(pejorative) A person who hoards money rather than spending it; one who is cheap or extremely parsimonious.
In a state of misery: very sad, ill, or poor.
Like a miser, very or objectionably cautious with money.

sense.def: Misery is easier to bear when one is not the only one miserable.
(uncountable) Bad luck.
(countable) An undesirable event such as an accident.
doubt, apprehension, a feeling of dread
An accident, mistake, or problem.
(ambitransitive) To hear wrongly.
To misunderstand.
(slang) Madness; silliness.
(literally) To lead astray, in a false direction.
Hatred of, contempt for, or prejudice against women.
(uncountable) The act of mispronouncing.
(countable) A mispronounced word or phrase.
An unmarried woman; a girl.
To miss an experience or lose an opportunity, etc. that should not be missed.
