(fatty acid) One of the most common saturated fatty acids; it is found in all animal and most vegetable oils and fats; it is used in the manufacture of soap etc.
An abnormal beating of the heart that may be perceived by the patient, a result of excitement, exertion, or illness.
Trashy, trivial, of little value.

A small, brief printed work, consisting either of a folded sheet of paper, or several sheets bound together into a booklet with only a paper cover, formerly containing literary compositions, newsletters, and newspapers, but now chiefly informational matter.
A wide, flat receptacle used around the house, especially for cooking.
Short for salt pan: a flat artificial pond used for collecting minerals from evaporated water.
The belief in unification of the peoples and countries of the Arab World.
A remedy believed to cure all disease and prolong life that was originally sought by alchemists; a cure-all.
A solution to all problems.
A thin batter cake fried in a pan or on a griddle in oil or butter; in particular:

(anatomy) A gland near the stomach which secretes a fluid into the duodenum to help with food digestion. The fluid contains protease, carbohydrase and lipase, which breaks down larger molecules into smaller pieces. The pancreas also produces the hormones insulin and glucagon which regulate blood sugar. These hormones are released into the cardiovascular system.
(colloquial, also, attributively) Short for giant panda (“Ailuropoda melanoleuca”). [from 19th c.]
(by extension, rare) Also in the plural form pandects: a comprehensive collection of laws; specifically, the whole body of law of a country; a legal code.

(religion) A belief in a god who is both pantheistic and deistic, in particular a god who designed the universe and then became it and ceased to exist separately and act consciously with respect to it.
(epidemiology) A pandemic disease; a disease that affects a wide geographical area and a large proportion of the population.
A loud, wild, tumultuous protest, disorder, or chaotic situation, usually of a crowd, often violent.
An outburst; loud, riotous uproar, especially of a crowd.
(intransitive) To tempt with, to appeal or cater to (improper motivations, etc.); to assist in gratification.
A formal speech publicly praising someone or something.
A group of people gathered to judge, interview, discuss etc. as on a television or radio broadcast for example.
(philosophy, religion) A doctrine that the universe subsists within God, but that God nevertheless transcends or has some existence separate from the universe.
A soft Italian sourdough brioche from Milan, with candied fruit, usually prepared for Christmas as a dessert.
(often, in the plural) A paroxysm of extreme physical pain or anguish; a feeling of sudden and transitory agony; a throe.
The scaly anteater; any of several long-tailed, scale-covered mammals of the order Pholidota of tropical Africa and Asia, the sole extant genus of which is Manis.
A sentence that contains every letter of the alphabet.
(US) To beg for money, especially with a container in hand for receiving loose change, especially on the street, and particularly, as a bum.
(uncountable) Overwhelming fear or fright, often affecting groups of people or animals; (countable) an instance of this; a fright, a scare.
To cause (someone) to feel panic; also, to frighten (someone) into acting hastily.
A sudden period of intense anxiety, mounting physiological arousal, fear, stomach problems and discomfort that are associated with a variety of somatic and cognitive symptoms.
(botany) A compound raceme.
A splendid display of something. [from 1829]
(historical) A complete set of armour. [from 1570s]
An unbroken view of an entire surrounding area.
A picture or series of pictures representing a continuous scene.
(figuratively) A comprehensive survey.

(musical instrument) An instrument consisting of a series of ten or more tubes of different lengths, typically closed at the bottom and open at the top. The instrument is played by blowing across the open end at the top.
A cultivated flowering plant, derived by hybridization within species Viola tricolor.
(derogatory, colloquial) A timid, weak man or boy; a wuss.
(ambitransitive) To breathe quickly or in a labored manner, as after exertion or from eagerness or excitement; to respire with heaving of the breast; to gasp.
An article of clothing covering each leg separately, that covers the area from the waist to the ankle.
(religion) The belief that the Universe is in some sense divine and should be revered. Pantheism identifies the universe with God but denies any personality or transcendence of such a God.
Any of various big cats with black fur; most especially, the black-coated leopard of Africa and Asia.
Any big cat of the genus Panthera.
Underpants for women and girls.
A mechanical linkage based on parallelograms causing two objects to move in parallel; notably as a drawing aid.
(rail transport) A similarly-formed conductive device, now usually Z-shaped, that collects electric current from overhead lines for trains and trams.
A small room, closet, or cabinet usually located in or near the kitchen, dedicated to shelf-stable food storage and/or storing kitchenware, like a larder, but smaller.

(chiefly, North America, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, India, Philippines) An outer garment that covers the body from the waist downwards, covering each leg separately, usually as far as the ankles; trousers. [from 19th c.]
(chiefly, UK) An undergarment that covers the genitals and often the buttocks and the neighbouring parts of the body; underpants. [from 19th c.]
A freelance photographer who sells photographs of celebrities to the media, especially one who pursues celebrities and attempts to obtain candid photographs.
The fruit of this tree.
Made of paper.
A sheet material typically used for writing on or printing on (or as a non-waterproof container), usually made by draining cellulose fibres from a suspension in water.
A written document, generally shorter than a book (white paper, term paper), in particular one written for the Government.
(US) A toy airplane made by folding up a sheet of paper.
The 1st anniversary of some event, particularly a wedding.
A small, folded, wire or plastic device used to hold sheets of paper together.
A disposable cup made out of paper and often lined with plastic or wax to prevent liquid from leaking out or soaking through the paper.
A factory devoted to making paper from wood pulp and other ingredients.
Cash in the form of banknotes.
(idiomatic) A seemingly fierce or powerful person, country or organisation without the ability to back up their words; apparently powerful but actually ineffective.
(Britain) A sheet of absorbent paper dispensed in restrooms, usually used for drying washed hands.
A small, decorative, somewhat weighty object placed on one or more pieces of paper to keep them from fluttering away.
Any object used for this purpose.
routine work involving written documents
(anatomy) A nipple-like protuberance on a part or organ of the body.
A bright reddish orange colour resembling that of the ground spice.
(usually, uncountable) A plant (Cyperus papyrus) in the sedge family, native to the Nile river valley, paper reed.
(usually, uncountable) A material similar to paper made from the papyrus plant.
(countable) A scroll or document written on papyrus.
(idiomatic) To be expected; normal; common.
A short narrative illustrating a lesson (usually religious/moral) by comparison or analogy.

(geometry) The conic section formed by the intersection of a cone with a plane parallel to a tangent plane to the cone; the locus of points equidistant from a fixed point (the focus) and line (the directrix).
(aviation) A device, generally constructed from fabric, that is designed to employ air resistance to control the fall of an object or person, causing them to float instead of falling.
The sport or activity of jumping with a parachute.
A public procession, especially one commemorating a holiday or special event or (dated) in protest.
A pattern, a way of doing something, especially a pattern of thought, a system of beliefs, a conceptual framework.
(linguistics) A set of all forms which contain a common element, especially the set of all inflectional forms of a word or a particular grammatical category.
(figuratively) A very pleasant place, such as a place full of lush vegetation.
(figuratively) A very pleasant experience.
(slang) The upper gallery in a theatre.
An apparently self-contradictory statement, which can only be true if it is false, and vice versa.
(uncountable, philosophy) A state in which one is logically compelled to contradict oneself.
The complete equipment used for paragliding, consisting of a paraglider wing and a harness.
The sport of gliding with a paraglider.
A person of preeminent qualities, who acts as a pattern or model for others. [from 16th c.]
A passage in text that starts on a new line, the first line sometimes being indented, and usually marks a change of topic.
(originally) A mark or note set in the margin to call attention to something in the text, such as a change of subject.
Any of various species of small parrot primarily of tropical regions. [from 16th c.]
Equally distant from one another at all points.
Having the same overall direction; the comparison is indicated with "to".
(sciences, scifi, cosmology) A universe that exists separately alongside another universe, as part of a multiverse.
(geometry) A solid figure, having six faces, all parallelograms, all opposite faces being similar and parallel.
(geometry) A convex quadrilateral in which each pair of opposite edges are parallel and of equal length.
An oval-shaped protozoan organism of the genus Paramecium.
A value kept constant during an experiment, equation, calculation, or similar, but varied over other versions of the experiment, equation, calculation, etc.
(often, postpositive) Highest, supreme; also, chief, leading, pre-eminent.
Of the highest importance.
(somewhat, archaic) An illicit lover, either male or female.

The obsolete name for a psychotic disorder, now called delusional disorder, often (in one of 6 subtypes) characterized by delusions of persecution and perceived threat against the individual affected with the disorder, and often associated with false accusations and general mistrust of others
Extreme, irrational distrust of others.
That (ostensibly) cannot be explained by what scientists know; supernatural; especially of or pertaining to ghosts, spirits, and supposed abilities like telepathy.
A low protective wall.
(military) A fortification consisting of a wall.

(sexology) Sexual arousal in response to sexual objects or situations which may interfere with the capacity for reciprocal affectionate sexual activity or lead to clinically significant distress or impairment (e.g. are obligatory, require participation of unconsenting individuals, lead to legal issues).
The study of alleged paranormal phenomena; psychic or occult phenomena, such as telepathy and ghosts.

(biology) An organism that lives on or in another organism of a different species, deriving benefit from living on or in that other organism, while not contributing towards that other organism sufficiently to cover the cost to that other organism.
(pejorative) A person who lives on other people's efforts or expense and gives little or nothing back. [from 16th c.]
Drawing upon another organism for sustenance.
A study of parasites.
A small light umbrella used as protection from the sun.
A package wrapped for shipment.
To wrap something up into the form of a package.
(transitive) To dry to extremity; to shrivel with heat.
(transitive, colloquial) To make very thirsty.
Very thirsty.
A document made on such material.
Stiff paper imitating that material.
Often used when someone does not understand what another person says.
Forgiveness for an offence.

(legal) An order that releases a convicted criminal without further punishment, prevents future punishment, or (in some jurisdictions) removes an offence from a person's criminal record, as if it had never been committed.
(transitive) To forgive (a person).
(transitive, legal) To grant an official pardon for a crime.
(idiomatic) Sorry; said as an apology.
(psychology) The tendency to interpret a vague stimulus as something known to the observer, such as interpreting marks on Mars as canals, seeing shapes in clouds, or hearing hidden messages in music.
(anatomy) The functional tissue of an organ as distinguished from the connective and supporting tissue.
One of the two persons from whom one is immediately biologically descended; a mother or father. [from 15th c.]
A person who acts as a parent in rearing a child; a step-parent or adoptive parent.
The source or origin of something. [from 16th c.]
(biology) An organism from which a plant or animal is immediately biologically descended. [from 17th c.]
A clause, phrase or word which is inserted (usually for explanation or amplification) into a passage which is already grammatically complete, and usually marked off with brackets, commas or dashes.
Either of a pair of brackets, especially (mainly US) round brackets, ( and ) (used to enclose parenthetical material in a text).
(rhetoric) A digression; the use of such digressions.
Gypsum.
(anatomy) Either of two bones that together form the sides and top of the skull.
In the Anglican, Eastern Orthodox, Lutheran and Roman Catholic Church, an administrative part of a diocese that has its own church.
The community attending that church; the members of the parish.

(US) An ecclesiastical society, usually not bounded by territorial limits, but composed of those persons who choose to unite under the charge of a particular priest, clergyman, or minister; also, loosely, the territory in which the members of a congregation live.
A civil subdivision of a British county, often corresponding to an earlier ecclesiastical parish.
A member of a parish.
An area of land set aside for environment preservation or recreation.
(transitive) To bring (something such as a vehicle) to a halt or store in a specified place.
(clothing) A long jacket with a hood which protects the wearer against rain and wind.
The action of the verb to park.
Space in which to park a car or other vehicle.
(North America, Philippines, Malaysia) An open area, generally paved, where automobiles may be left when not in use.
A device, located by a parking space, that collects payment in exchange for the right to park a vehicle for a specified time.
A legal summons issued for parking a motor vehicle in a place where such parking is restricted, or beyond the time paid for.

(sport) An athletic discipline, in which practitioners traverse any environment in the most efficient way possible using their physical abilities, and which commonly involves running, jumping, vaulting, rolling, flipping, and other similar physical movements.
(dated) A path, carriage-way, or road through a park or a landscaped right of way.
A certain way of speaking, of using words; especially that associated with a particular job or interest.

In many countries, the legislative branch of government, a deliberative assembly or set of assemblies whose elected or appointed members meet to debate the major political issues of the day, make, amend, and repeal laws, authorize the executive branch of government to spend money, and in some cases exercise judicial powers; a legislature. [from 14th c.]

A particular assembly of the members of such a legislature, as convened for a specific purpose or period of time (commonly designated with an ordinal number – for example, first parliament or 12th parliament – or a descriptive adjective – for example, Long Parliament, Short Parliament and Rump Parliament). [from 14th c.]
(Commonwealth) A member of a parliament, congress or an elected national legislative body of another name.
Of, relating to, or enacted by a parliament.
(dated, except in, Mid-Atlantic US) The living room of a house, or a room for entertaining guests; a room for talking; a sitting-room or drawing room.
A shop or other business selling goods or services specified by context.
A hard, full-fat Italian cheese from Parma.
Characterized by an unsophisticated focus on local concerns to the exclusion of wider contexts; elementary in scope or outlook.
A work or performance that imitates another work or performance with ridicule or irony.
(countable, archaic) A popular maxim, adage, or proverb.
(pathology) A distorted sense of smell, often resulting in the apparent detection of non-existent smells which are mostly unpleasant.
A kind of bird, many species of which are colorful and able to mimic human speech, of the order Psittaciformes or (narrowly) of the family Psittacidae.
(metaphorical) A parroter; a person who repeats the words or ideas of others.
To avoid, deflect, or ward off (an attack, a blow, an argument, etc.).
(computing, linguistics) An act of parsing; a parsing.

(linguistics, ambitransitive) To resolve (a sentence, etc.) into its elements, pointing out the several parts of speech, and their relation to each other by agreement or government; to analyze and describe grammatically. [from mid 16th c.]
(astronomy, metrology) Short for parallax second.
(computing) A computer program that parses.
Exhibiting parsimony; sparing in the expenditure of money; frugal to excess.
(by extension) The quality or characteristic of using the fewest resources or explanations to solve a problem.
(countable, uncountable) A bright green, biennial herb, Petroselinum crispum, having many cultivars.
A biennial plant, Pastinaca sativa, related to the carrot.
The root of the parsnip, when used as a vegetable.
A fraction of a whole.
A group inside a larger group.
Position or role (especially in a play).
(transitive) To divide in two.
(intransitive) To be divided in two or separated.
To end a relationship. [with with]
(grammar) A linguistic category of words sharing syntactic or morphological behaviour and semantic properties, such as noun or verb.
To go in different directions.
(formal) To take part in an activity; to participate. [with in]
existing as a part or portion; incomplete
(mathematics) of or relating to a partial derivative or partial differential
To a partial degree or extent, incompletely.
(intransitive) To join in, to take part, to involve oneself (in something). [from 16th c.]
The act of participating, of taking part in something.

(political science) A form of government in which citizens participate individually and directly in political decisions and policies affecting their lives, rather than through elected representatives.

(grammar) A form of a verb that may function as an adjective, noun or adverb. English has two types of participles: the present participle and the past participle. In other languages, there are others, such as future, perfect, and future perfect participles.
A very small piece of matter, a fragment; especially, the smallest possible part of something. [from 14th c.]
(physics) Any of various physical objects making up the constituent parts of an atom; an elementary particle or subatomic particle. [from 19th c.]
A device that accelerates electrically charged particles to extremely high speeds, for the purpose of inducing high energy reactions or producing high energy radiation.
Specific; discrete; concrete.
(comparable) Of a person, concerned with, or attentive to, details; fastidious.
Concerned with, or attentive to, details; minute; circumstantial; precise.
Specialised; characteristic of a specific person or thing.
Distinguished in some way; special (often in negative constructions).
A farewell, the act of departing politely.
A fervent, sometimes militant, supporter or proponent of a party, cause, faction, person, or idea.
That which divides or separates; that by which different things, or distinct parts of the same thing, are separated; boundary; dividing line or space.
In part, or to some degree, but not completely.
A member of a business or law partnership.
A spouse or other person with whom one shares a domestic, romantic or sexual bond.
Someone who is associated with another in a common activity or interest.
Someone with whom one dances in a two-person dance.
Someone with whom one plays on the same side in a game, such as card games or doubles tennis.
(nautical) One of the pieces of wood comprising the framework which strengthens the deck of a wooden ship around the holes through which the mast and other fittings pass.
(Jamaica) A group financial arrangement in which each member contributes a set amount of money over a set period.
An association of two or more people to conduct a business
(ornithology) Any bird of a number of genera in the family Phasianidae, notably in the genera Perdix and Alectoris.
The act of giving birth; childbirth.
(legal) A person or group of people constituting a particular side in a contract or legal action.
(now, rare, _, in general sense) A group of people forming one side in a given dispute, contest etc.
A gathering of acquaintances so that one of them may offer items for sale to the rest of them.
membership card of a political party
A step in a dance. [from 18th c.]
In the International System of Units, the derived unit of pressure and stress; one newton per square metre. Symbol: Pa.
An opening, road, or track, available for passing; especially, one through or over some dangerous or otherwise impracticable barrier such as a mountain range; a passageway; a defile; a ford.
A single passage of a tool over something, or of something over a tool.
A document granting permission to pass or to go and come; a passport; a ticket permitting free transit or admission
(ditransitive) To cause to move or go; to send; to transfer from one person, place, or condition to another.
(transitive) To go past, by, over, or through; to proceed from one side to the other of; to move past.

(transitive) To cause to advance by stages of progress; to carry on with success through an ordeal, examination, or action; specifically, to give legal or official sanction to; to ratify; to enact; to approve as valid and just.
(transitive) To transcend; to surpass; to excel; to exceed.
(transitive) To go by without noticing; to omit attention to; to take no note of; to disregard.
(archaic, literary) To disappear; to cease to be; to be no more.
(transitive) To hand over, pass through or transfer to a lower level, next generation, etc.
To convey or communicate.
(transitive) To distribute, to hand out.
(idiomatic, informal) To transfer responsibility or blame from oneself onto another; to absolve oneself of concern for a given matter by claiming to lack authority or jurisdiction.
A ticket (or similar) allowing a person to leave (a theatre etc) and subsequently re-enter
Tolerable; adequate; no more than satisfactory.
A paragraph or section of text or music with particular meaning.
A passageway or corridor.
A covered walkway, between rooms or buildings.
A string of characters used for authentication on a digital device.
One who rides or travels in a vehicle, but who does not operate it and is not a member of the crew.
(automotive) A seat in a vehicle for a passenger, especially the front seat next to the driver in a motor vehicle.
A person who is passing by (that is, walking past).
Any bird of the order Passeriformes, which comprises more than half of all bird species.
That passes away; ephemeral. [from 14th c.]
(now, _, rare, literary) Pre-eminent, excellent, extreme. [from 14th c.]
Vague, cursory. [from 18th c.]
(literary, or, archaic) Surpassingly, greatly. [from 14th c.]
Death, dying; the end of something. [from 14th c.]
The fact of going past; a movement from one place to another or a change from one state to another. [from 14th c.]
Any great, strong, powerful emotion, especially romantic love or extreme hate.
An object of passionate or romantic love or strong romantic interest.
(uncountable) The flesh of the edible fruit.
Any of very many vines, in North America and elsewhere, of the genus Passiflora that bear edible fruit called passion fruit, and showy flowers of a structure symbolic of the Passion of Christ.
(chemistry, materials science) The process of making a material passive (non-reactive) in relation to another material prior to using the materials together.
Being subjected to an action without producing a reaction.
(grammar) Being in the passive voice.
A key for entering a house or other building.
An official document normally used for international journeys, which proves the identity and nationality of the person for whom it was issued.
(military, security) A word relayed to a person to gain admittance to a place or to gain access to information.

(computing, cryptography) A string of characters used to log in to a computer or network, to access a level in a video game, and so on; archetypally a word#Noun but nowadays often an alphanumeric#Adjective string or a phrase#Noun.
Having already happened; in the past; finished. [from 14th c.]
The period of time that has already happened, in contrast to the present and the future.

(grammar) A grammatical form (often a verb form) that refers to an event, transaction, occurrence, or object that happened (or had happened), or existed, at some time before now (the applicable reference time).
(uncountable) Dough made from wheat and water and sometimes mixed with egg and formed into various shapes; often sold in dried form and typically boiled for eating.
A soft moist mixture, in particular:
One of flour, fat, or similar ingredients used in making pastry.
One of pounded foods, such as fish paste, liver paste, or tomato paste.
A crayon made from such a paste.
(British spelling) Heat-treatment of a perishable food to destroy heat-sensitive vegetative cells followed by immediate cooling to limit growth of the surviving cells and germination of spores.
(transitive) To heat food for the purpose of killing harmful organisms such as bacteria, viruses, protozoa, molds, and yeasts.
An item worn (often by strippers) to conceal one's nipples.
An often round and somewhat flat flavoured candy or sweet.
Any small, usually round and somewhat flat, granular piece of material; a tablet.
(historical) A medicinal pill, originally made of compressed herbs.
Something which amuses, and serves to make time pass agreeably.
(Protestantism) A minister or priest in a church.
A seasoned smoked cut of beef. Traditionally, this is made from a navel cut.
(uncountable) The food group formed by the various kinds of pastries.
Land, specifically, an open field, on which livestock is kept for feeding.
(chiefly, _, in the plural) A small item of clothing that conceals little more than the nipple of a woman's breast, primarily worn by female exotic dancers.
Trite, being superficially complete, lacking originality.
A light tap or slap, especially with the hands
(specifically) A small area, a small plot of land or piece of ground.
To mend by sewing on a piece or pieces of cloth, leather, or the like.
Any of several East Indian plants in the genus Pogostemon, especially Pogostemon cablin, which yield a highly fragrant oil.
The oil or perfume made from these plants.
Explicit and obvious.
A declaration issued by a government agency that the inventor of a new invention has the sole privilege of making, selling, or using the claimed invention for a specified period.
In a clear and unambiguous manner.
A sister of someone’s father.
The wife of a sibling of someone’s father.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see paternal,‎ grandfather. (This entry is a translation hub.)
A brother or brother-in-law of one's father. (This entry is a translation hub.)
(archaic) A patent medicine, so named because salesmen would pray the Lord's Prayer over it before selling it.
A trail for the use of, or worn by, pedestrians.
A course taken.
(computing) A human-readable specification for a location within a hierarchical or tree-like structure, such as a file system or as part of a URL.

(graph theory) A sequence of vertices from one vertex to another using the arcs (edges). A path does not visit the same vertex more than once (unless it is a closed path, where only the first and the last vertex are the same).
(topology) A continuous map f from the unit interval I = [0,1] to a topological space X.
Arousing pity, sympathy, or compassion; exciting pathos.
(academic, _, medicine) The academic biomedical specialty that advances the aspects of the biomedical sciences that allow for those clinical applications and their advancements over time.
Pathosis: any deviation from a healthy or normal structure or function; abnormality; illness or malformation.
The quality of being patient.
(of a person) Willing to wait if necessary; not losing one's temper while waiting.
A person or animal who receives treatment from a doctor or other medically educated person.
A paved outside area, adjoining a house, used for dining or recreation.
(UK) a shop that sells pastries and cakes

(Christianity) The highest form of bishop, in the ancient world having authority over other bishops in the province but now generally as an honorary title; in Roman Catholicism, considered a bishop second only to the Pope in rank. [from 9th c.]
The male head of a household or nuclear family.
A person who loves and zealously supports and defends their country.
Love of one's country; devotion to the welfare of one's compatriots; passion which inspires one to serve one's country.
(transitive) To go the rounds of, as a sentry, guard, or policeman
(Christianity) A saint conceived as the patron (protector or supporter) of a particular place, group, person, or activity, for whom or for which his or her intercession is specially invoked.
The name of someone's father.
A patronymic surname.
Derived from one's father.
(by extension) Derived from one's ancestors.

(by extension) A name acquired from one's father's, grandfather's or earlier (male) ancestor's first name. Some cultures use a patronymic where other cultures use a surname or family name; other cultures (like Russia) use both a patronymic and a surname.
(informal, derogatory) A person who is taken advantage of, especially by being cheated or blamed for something.
Glib and rapid speech, such as from an auctioneer or a sports commentator.
Something from which a copy is made; a model or outline. [from 14th c.]
(textiles) The paper or cardboard template from which the parts of a garment are traced onto fabric prior to cutting out and assembling.
A design, motif or decoration, especially formed from regular repeated elements. [from 16th c.]
Fewness in number; too few.
A component of plate armor that protects the shoulder, generally covering more than a spaulder, also protecting the armpit and overlapping with other armor over the upper chest and back.
The first compartment of the stomach of a ruminant, the rumen.
The belly of a human, especially a large, fat protruding one.
One who is extremely poor.
One living on or eligible for public charity.
A temporary stop or rest; an intermission of action; interruption; suspension; cessation.
(British) To cover something with paving slabs.
(Canada, US) To cover with stone, concrete, blacktop or other solid covering, especially to aid travel.
(now, chiefly, North America) A paving (paved part) of a road or other thoroughfare; the roadway or road surface. [from 13th c.]
An ornate tent.
A light roofed structure used as a shelter in a public place.
A structure, sometimes temporary, erected to house exhibits at a fair, etc.
A detached or semi-detached building at a hospital or other building complex.
The soft foot of a mammal or other animal, generally a quadruped, that has claws or nails; comparable to a human hand or foot.
(chess) The most numerous chess piece, or a similar piece in a similar game. In chess, each side starts with eight; moves are only forward, and attacks are only diagonally or en passant.
(figurative) Someone who is being manipulated or used to some end.
(rare) A pawnshop; pawnbroker.
A person who makes monetary loans at interest, taking personal property as security – which may be sold if not redeemed.
The business premises of a pawnbroker; where loans are made, with personal property as security
(UK, dated, school slang) A cry for peace or truce in children's games.
(transitive) To give money or other compensation to in exchange for goods or services.
(ambitransitive) To discharge, as a debt or other obligation, by giving or doing what is due or required.
(intransitive) To discharge an obligation or debt.
(intransitive) To suffer consequences.
(transitive) To be profitable for.
(idiomatic, intransitive) To attend; to be attentive; to focus one's attention.
(figuratively) To avenge, to exact revenge.
(intransitive) To become worthwhile; to produce a net benefit.
(transitive) To pay back (repay) the entirety of a loan, thereby effecting the release of a lien on (the thing that was financed).
A reward.
(uncountable) An act of revenge.
(uncountable) The act of paying.
(countable) An instance of that act; a sum of money paid in exchange#Noun for goods or services, or the transaction#Noun that conveys it.
An amount of money paid out.

(intransitive) To flow or move forward rapidly or noisily.
The deteriorated state of iron or steel as a result of moisture and oxidation.
A reddish-brown color.
A disease of plants caused by a reddish-brown fungus.
Unfinished or roughly finished.
(now, North America) The edible root of this plant
A metallic chemical element (symbol Ru) with an atomic number of 44.
A transuranic chemical element (symbol Rf) with an atomic number of 104.
Without pity or compassion; cruel, pitiless.
(mineral) The most frequent of the three polymorphs of titanium dioxide, crystalizing in the tetragonal system, TiO2.
The grass Secale cereale from which the grain is obtained. [from 14th c.]
An extended period of leave from a person's usual pursuits.
Of the black colour sable.
(tincture) : In blazon, of the colour black.
(tincture) A black colour on a coat of arms (Wikipedia).
(countable, and, uncountable) A dark brown colour, resembling the fur of some sables.
A carrier around a projectile in a firearm, cannon or other type of artillery piece that precisely holds the projectile within the barrel.

(figurative, derogatory) Excessively sweet in action or disposition, especially if romantic or sentimental to the point of ridiculousness; sickly sweet, syrupy.

A bag; especially a large bag of strong, coarse material for storage and handling of various commodities, such as potatoes, coal, coffee; or, a bag with handles used at a supermarket, a grocery sack; or, a small bag for small items, a satchel.
(informal) Dismissal from employment, or discharge from a position.
(colloquial, US, literally, or, figurative) Bed.
(informal, transitive) To discharge from a job or position; to fire.
(anatomy) Of the sacrum.
Sacred.
(Christianity) A sacred act and the attendant ceremony, considered (theology) an outward sign of divine grace.
Characterized by solemn religious ceremony or religious use, especially, in a positive sense; consecrated, made holy.
A human being or an animal, or a physical object or immaterial thing (see sense 1.3), offered to a deity.
(baseball) A play in which the batter intentionally hits the ball softly with a hands-spread batting stance at the cost of an out to advance one or more runners.
Desecration, profanation, misuse or violation of something regarded as sacred.
(dated, or, jocular, hyperforeign) An expression of surprise, exasperation, or dismay; good heavens; oh my gosh.
Feeling sorrow; sorrowful, mournful.
Causing sorrow; lamentable.
Poor in quality, bad; shameful, deplorable; later, regrettable, poor.
(slang) Unfashionable; socially inadequate or undesirable.
A seat for a rider, typically made of leather and raised in the front and rear, placed on the back of a horse or other animal, and secured by a strap around the animal's body.
The immovable seat of a bicycle, motorcycle, or similar vehicle.
Achievement of sexual gratification by inflicting pain or humiliation on others, or watching pain or humiliation inflicted on others.
(uncountable) The state or emotion of being sad.
The practices of sadism and masochism collectively, usually in reference to consensual practices within the BDSM community.
Sadism and masochism: the (often sexual) enjoyment by one person of both inflicting and receiving pain.
Not in danger; out of harm's reach.
Free from risk.
Providing protection from danger; providing shelter.
Having come to no harm, especially after being exposed to danger.
Something that serves as a guard or protection; a defense.
The condition or feeling of being safe; security; certainty.
(sewing) A pin in the form of a clasp, which has a guard to cover the sharp point; used to join two pieces of fabric, etc., together temporarily.
A spice (seasoning) and colouring agent made from the stigma and part of the style of the plant, sometimes or formerly also used as a dye and insect repellent.
Lactarius deliciosus, an edible mushroom native to Europe.
The difference in elevation of a wire, cable, chain or rope suspended between two consecutive points.
(by extension) To lean, give way, or settle from a vertical position.

(figuratively) To lose firmness, elasticity, vigor, or a thriving state; to sink; to droop; to flag; to bend; to yield, as the mind or spirits, under the pressure of care, trouble, doubt, or the like; to be unsettled or unbalanced.
An Old Norse (Icelandic) prose narrative, especially one dealing with family or social histories and legends.
Something with the qualities of such a saga; an epic, a long story.
The quality of being sage, wise, or able to make good decisions; the quality of being perceptive, astute or insightful.
Wise.
A wise person or spiritual teacher; someone of gravity and wisdom, especially, a teacher venerable for years, and of sound judgment and prudence; a grave or stoic philosopher.
The plant Salvia officinalis and savory spice produced from it; also planted for ornamental purposes.
Any plant in the genus Salvia.
A large grouse of western North America having mottled gray, black and buff plumage (Centrocercus urophasianus) which feeds on the buds of the sagebrush.
(nautical) A piece of fabric attached to a boat and arranged such that it causes the wind to drive the boat along. The sail may be attached to the boat via a combination of mast, spars and ropes.
A recreational device consisting of a surfboard with a small sail on a flexible mast.
A boat propelled by a sail.
Motion across a body of water in a craft powered by the wind, as a sport or otherwise
In particular, a member of the crew of a (civilian or military) vessel, as opposed to a captain, admiral, etc.; a mariner; a common seaman.
(religion, generally) A deceased person whom a church or another religious group has officially recognised as especially holy or godly; one eminent for piety and virtue.
(Mormonism, specifically) Alternative letter-case form of Saint (“a Mormon, a Latter-day Saint”)
(figuratively, by extension) A person with similarly overwhelming positive qualities; one who does good.
cause, interest or account
the benefit or regard of someone or something
cherry blossom (blossom of the Japanese cherry tree)
Rice wine; a drink made from filtered fermented rice.
Shorea robusta, a dipterocarpaceous tree.
Lascivious, bawdy, obscene, lewd.
A food made primarily of a mixture of raw or cold ingredients, typically vegetables, usually served with a dressing such as vinegar or mayonnaise.
A long, slender, chiefly terrestrial amphibian of the order Caudata, superficially resembling a lizard.
(economics) Salary earners as a class or group, often as opposed to wage earners.
A fixed amount of money paid to a worker, usually calculated on a monthly or annual basis, not hourly, as wages. Implies a degree of professionalism and/or autonomy.
(Islam) The obligatory prayer that Muslims are called to perform five times a day.

(pharmaceutical drug) A synthetic beta-agonist bronchodilator related to aspirin, administered in the form of its sulfate (C13H21NO3)2·H2SO4 as an inhalational aerosol or as a tablet to treat bronchospasm associated especially with asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. It is marketed under the trademarks Combivent, Proventil and Ventolin.
An exchange of goods or services for currency or credit.
The act of putting up for auction to the highest bidder.
A man whose job it is to sell things, either in a shop/store or elsewhere.

A European willow, Salix caprea, that has broad leaves, large catkins and tough wood.
A sortie of troops from a besieged place against an enemy.
An excursion or side trip.
A meal or dish made from this fish.

Any of the serotypes of the two species of rod-shaped bacteria, of the genus Salmonella, especially Salmonella enterica, that cause typhoid fever and salmonellosis, manifest as food poisoning and other diseases.
a type of fatback, or non-rendered underskin pig fat consumed in Central and Eastern Europe, usually seasoned
A large room, especially one used to receive and entertain guests.
A beauty salon or similar establishment.
A common substance, chemically consisting mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl), used extensively as a condiment and preservative.
(chemistry) One of the compounds formed from the reaction of an acid with a base, where a positive ion replaces a hydrogen of the acid.
A landlocked body of water with a high concentration of salts and other dissolved minerals.

sense.def: (idiomatic) A person or group of people considered to represent the most decent and admirable parts of humanity.

A part or snippet of something taken or presented for inspection, or shown as evidence of the quality of the whole; a specimen.

Making a show of being morally better than others, especially hypocritically pious.

The California sardine Sardinops sagax (syn. Clupea sagax) is similar. The American sardines of the Atlantic coast are mostly the young of the Atlantic herring and of the menhaden.

Scornfully mocking or cynical.
A brown alga, of the genus Sargassum, that forms large, floating masses.

The traditional dress of women in the Indian Subcontinent; an outer garment consisting of a single length of cotton or silk, most often with one end wrapped around the waist to form a skirt, the other draped over the shoulder or head.
A camellia, Camellia sasanqua, native to China and Japan.
A decorative length of cloth worn over the shoulder to the opposite hip, often for ceremonial or other formal occasions.
A dish consisting of thin slices or pieces of raw fish or meat.

(military, historical, army) A body of cavalry comprising two companies or troops, averaging from one hundred and twenty to two hundred soldiers.
(military, navy) A detachment of vessels employed on any particular service or station, under the command of the senior officer
(military, air force) A tactical air force unit; consists of at least two flights; multiple squadrons make up a group or wing (depending on particular air force).
(organic compound) A linear triterpene hydrocarbon found in shark liver oil and in human sebum; it plays a role in the biosynthesis of steroids.
Extremely dirty and unpleasant.
(often, nautical) A sudden storm, as found in a squall line.
To waste, lavish, splurge; to spend lavishly or profusely; to dissipate.
Shaped like a square (the polygon).
Used in the names of units of area formed by multiplying a unit of length by itself.
(printing) A certain number of lines, forming a portion of a column, nearly square; used chiefly in reckoning the prices of advertisements in newspapers.
(mathematics) The product of a number or quantity multiplied by itself; the second power of a number, value, term or expression.
Either of a pair of symbols, [ ], used for various purposes, e.g. to enclose text inserted or replaced by an editor, and to indicate various mathematical operations.
(geometry) A unit of solid angle equal to π²/32400 steradians
Standard unit of area, symbol km2, equal to the area of a square whose sides are one kilometre long; 106 square metres.
A standard unit of area equal to the area of a square whose sides are one metre long (that is, an area one meter square) Symbol: m2
(mathematics) The number which, when squared, yields another number.
(mathematics) Raised to the second power.
(figurative) In a direct, straightforward and honest manner.
(botany, countable) A plant and its fruit of any of a few species of the genus Cucurbita, or gourd kind.
A building occupied without permission, as practiced by a squatter.
To sit close to the ground; to stoop, or lie close to the ground, for example to escape observation.
(intransitive, slang) To give sensitive information about someone to a third party; to rat on someone.
(transitive) Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see squeeze,‎ out.
(slang) Engendering a feeling of disgust, distaste, nausea or revulsion, but without a judgment regarding the rightness or wrongness of the stimulus.
Any of several carnivorous marine cephalopod mollusks, of the order Teuthida, having a mantle, eight arms, and a pair of tentacles
A fishhook with a piece of bright lead, bone, or other substance fastened on its shank to imitate a squid.
(US, military, slang, mildly, pejorative) A sailor in the Navy.
(UK, slang, humorous, rare) A quid; one pound sterling.
(British, informal) slightly drunk or intoxicated; tipsy
An illegible scrawl.
(architecture) A structure constructed between two adjacent walls to aid in the transition from a polygonal to a circular structure, as when a dome is constructed on top of a square room.
A devoted attendant or follower of a lady; a beau.
To twist one's body with snakelike motions.
To twist in discomfort, especially from shame or embarrassment.
Any of the rodents of the family Sciuridae distinguished by their large bushy tail.
(UK, US, Australia, slang) A small child.
(transitive, informal) To squeeze, compress, or crush (especially something moist).
(of an object or substance) Yielding easily to pressure; very soft; especially, soft and wet, as mud.
Relatively unchanging, steady, permanent; firmly fixed or established; consistent; not easily moved, altered, or destroyed.
A building, wing or dependency set apart and adapted for lodging and feeding (and training) ungulates, especially horses.
In a stable manner.
A pile of similar objects, each directly on top of the last.
(computing, often with "the") A stack data structure stored in main memory that is manipulated during machine language procedure call related instructions.
A venue where sporting events are held.
(plural staffs or staves) A long, straight, thick wooden rod or stick, especially one used to assist in walking.
(engineering) An arbor, as of a wheel or a pinion of a watch.
(countable) An adult male deer, especially a red deer and especially one in high adulthood versus a young adult.
(countable) An improperly or late castrated bull or ram – also called a bull seg (see note under ox).
Any of numerous large beetles of the family Lucanidae, the males having elaborate mandibles resembling the antlers of a stag
especially, the largest beetle in the UK, of species Lucanus cervus.
A phase.
(by extension) One of the portions of a device (such as a rocket or thermonuclear weapon) which are used or activated in a particular order, one after another.
(video games) A level; one of the sequential areas making up the game.
(geology) The succession of rock strata laid down in a single age on the geologic time scale.
(dated) A place of rest on a regularly travelled road; a station; a place appointed for a relay of horses.
(electronics) The number of an electronic circuit’s block, such as a filter, an amplifier, etc.
The pseudonym of an entertainer.
An unsteady movement of the body in walking or standing as if one were about to fall; a reeling motion.
(intransitive) In standing or walking, to sway from one side to the other as if about to fall; to stand or walk unsteadily; to reel or totter.
A structure of posts and boards for supporting workmen, etc., as in building.
Not capricious or impulsive; sedate, serious, sober.
A discolored spot or area caused by spillage or other contact with certain fluids or substances.
A reagent or dye used to stain microscope specimens so as to make some structures visible.
Glass that has been coloured, either by painting or by fusing pigments into its structure.
Made of stainless steel.
An alloy of iron and chromium that resists corrosion.
A single step in a staircase.
A series of steps; a staircase.
A flight of stairs; a stairway.
A contiguous set of steps connecting two floors.
A set of steps, with or without a case, that allow one to walk up or down.
A shaft in a multi-story building enclosing a stairway or staircase.
A piece of wood or other material, usually long and slender, pointed at one end so as to be easily driven into the ground as a marker or a support or stay.
(with definite article) The piece of timber to which a person condemned to death was affixed to be burned.
A share or interest in a business or a given situation.
(geology) A secondary mineral deposit of calcium carbonate or another mineral, in shapes similar to icicles, that hangs from the roof of a cave.
(geology) A secondary mineral deposit of calcium carbonate or other mineral, in shapes similar to icicles, that lies on the ground of a cave.
No longer fresh, new, or interesting, in reference to ideas and immaterial things; clichéd, hackneyed, dated.
(chess) The state in which the player to move is not in check but has no legal moves, resulting in a draw.

(mathematics, sheaf theory) Informally, a construction which generalizes that of the notion of the ring of germs of functions near a point to the context of arbitrary sheaves. Formally, given a sheaf \mathcal{F} on a space X, and a point x in X, the direct limit of the sections of F on the open neighborhoods of x ordered by reverse inclusion. See w:Stalk (sheaf) on Wikipedia.Wikipedia
A stable; a place for cattle.
A bench or table on which small articles of merchandise are exposed for sale.
(countable) A small open-fronted shop, for example in a market, food court, etc.
(transitive, aviation) To cause to exceed the critical angle of attack, resulting in loss of lift.
A male horse kept primarily as a stud.
An adult male horse.
Firmly or solidly built.
Courageous.
One who firmly supports a cause.
(botany) In flowering plants, the structure in a flower that produces pollen, typically consisting of an anther and a filament.
The energy and strength for continuing to do something over a long period of time; power of sustained exertion, or resistance to hardship, illness etc.
An indentation, imprint, or mark made by stamping.
A device for stamping designs.
A small piece of paper bearing a design on one side and adhesive on the other, used to decorate letters or craft work.
The manner, pose, or posture in which one stands.
One's opinion or point of view.
A vertical pole, post, or support.
A defensive position or effort.
A resolute, unwavering position; firm opinion; action for a purpose in the face of opposition.
A device to hold something upright or aloft.
A small building, booth, or stage, as in a bandstand or hamburger stand.
(intransitive, copulative) To support oneself on the feet in an erect position.
(intransitive, copulative) To maintain one's ground; to be acquitted; not to fail or yield; to be safe.
(intransitive, followed by to + infinitive) To be positioned to gain or lose.
(intransitive) To rise to one’s feet; to stand up.
(idiomatic, intransitive) To wait in expectation of some event; to be ready.
To substitute for; to replace; (theater) to serve as an understudy.
(idiomatic, transitive) To replace; to act as a double or substitute for.
(intransitive) To rise from a lying or sitting position.
(transitive, idiomatic) (stand someone up) To avoid a prearranged meeting, especially a date, with (a person) without prior notification; to jilt or shirk.
The flag or ensign carried by a military unit.
(statistics) A measure of how spread out data values are around the mean, defined as the square root of the variance. Represented with the Greek letter σ.

A relative measure of the quality of life a person or group has, often with per capita income (GNI or GDP) serving as a proxy measurement but with some notion of human development as the real (underlying) entity being measured.
(figurative) Position or reputation in society or a profession.

(physics) A wave form which occurs in a limited, fixed medium in such a way that the reflected wave coincides with the produced wave. A common example is the vibration of the strings on a musical stringed instrument.
Point of view; perspective
a dark-gray lustrous mineral, a mixed sulfide of copper, iron, and tin, Cu2FeSnS4, used as an ore of tin
A unit of a poem, written or printed as a paragraph; equivalent to a verse.
A wire fastener used to secure stacks of paper by penetrating all the sheets and curling around.
The principal commodity produced in a town or region.
A device which binds together sheets of paper by driving a thin metal staple through the sheets and simultaneously folding over the ends of the staple against the back surface of the paper.
(geometry) A concave polygon with regular, pointy protrusions and indentations, usually with four, five, or six points.
(acting) An actor in a leading role.
A symbol used to rate hotels, films, etc. with a higher number of stars denoting better quality.
A composition of combustible matter used in the heading of rockets, in mines, etc., which, exploding in the air, presents a starlike appearance.

(networking) A network topology with multiple computers individually merging to one central switch, thus free of risk of collisions. A single point of failure can occur if the switch experiences corruption.
An exceptionally talented or famous person, often in a specific field; a celebrity.

A simple dance, or part of a dance, where a group of four dancers each put their right or left hand in the middle and turn around in a circle. You call them right-hand stars or left-hand stars, depending on the hand which is in the middle.

A plant, Illicium verum, used primarily for its star-shaped seed which resembles anise in scent and flavor, and which is used as a spice. Valued for its decorative shape as well as its flavor. Also used commercially as a source of shikimic acid for the production of Tamiflu.
(astronomy) A group of gravitationally bound stars and other material (such as nebulae and planets), conventionally with one generation of similarly aged stars from the same pre-stellar nebula.
(star) A group of stars (and possibly smaller bodies such as planets or asteroids) that orbit one another.
Any of the genus Ornithogalum of perennial plants mostly native to southern Europe and southern Africa, with clusters of typically white star-shaped flowers.

The righthand side of a ship, boat or aircraft when facing the front, or fore or bow. Used to unambiguously refer to directions according to the sides of the vessel, rather than those of a crew member or object.
(nutrition, countable) Carbohydrates, as with grain and potato based foods.
(countable) Any of various starch-like substances used as a laundry stiffener.
(intransitive, followed by "at") To look fixedly (at something).
(intransitive, obsolete) To stand out; to project; to bristle.
Any of various asteroids or other echinoderms (not in fact fish) with usually five arms, many of which eat bivalves or corals by everting their stomach.
(obsolete) Hard, firm; obdurate.
Severe; violent; fierce (now usually in describing the weather).
Plain in appearance; barren, desolate.
starkly; entirely, absolutely
Completely naked.
A family, Sturnidae, of passerine birds.
The beginning point of a race, a board game, etc.
(intransitive) To have its origin (at), begin.
(transitive) To disturb and cause to move suddenly; to startle; to alarm; to rouse; to cause to flee or fly.
An electric motor that starts an internal combustion engine.
A device that initiates the flow of high voltage electricity in a fluorescent lamp.
The first course of a meal, consisting of a small, usually savoury, dish.
(sometimes, figurative) The place where a journey starts.
The first steps when commencing an activity.
(transitive) To excite by sudden alarm, surprise, or apprehension; to frighten suddenly and not seriously; to alarm; to surprise.
Surprised and slightly frightened.
A new company or organization or business venture designed for rapid growth.
A condition of severe suffering due to a lack of nutrition.
(intransitive) To be very hungry.
(countable) A collection, sometimes hidden; a reserve.
(medicine) Immediately; now.
(computing) The set of all parameters relevant to a computation.
(computing) The stable condition of a processor during a particular clock cycle.
(computing) The values of all parameters at some point in a computation.
(anthropology) A society larger than a tribe. A society large enough to form a state in the sense of a government.
A political division of a federation retaining a notable degree of autonomy, as in the United States, Mexico, Nigeria, or India.
(mathematics, stochastic processes) An element of the range of the random variables that define a random process.
(transitive) To declare to be a fact.
The capital city of a state (national subdivision).
The form of capitalism where for-profit commercial activities are undertaken by the state; either via corporatized government agencies, or via ownership or control of nominally private organizations.
(idiomatic) A specific situation; a set of circumstances.
The overall physical condition of a person, as opposed to mental condition (state of mind).
(software, design) A behavioural design pattern similar to the strategy pattern that is used to represent the state of an object.
A formal visit by a head of state or a cabinet minister to another nation.
A declaration or remark.
A presentation of opinion or position.
(computing) An instruction in a computer program, especially one that returns no value, as opposed to a function call.
(uncountable) Interference on a broadcast signal caused by atmospheric disturbances; heard as crackles on radio, or seen as random specks on television.
An electric charge that has built up on an insulated body, often due to friction.
The electric discharge from such a body.
A place where one performs a task or where one is on call to perform a task.
Writing materials, envelopes, office materials.

(rail) The person in charge of a railroad station, usually an employee of a particular railroad by which the station is owned, but sometimes an employee of a separate corporation, such as one owning a station used by two or more railroads.
(archaic) A skilled politician or one with political power, knowledge or influence. [from 16th c.]
A person who compiles, interprets, or studies statistics.
A discipline, principally within applied mathematics, concerned with the systematic study of the collection, presentation, analysis, and interpretation of data.
A systematic collection of data on measurements or observations, often related to demographic information such as population counts, incomes, population counts at different ages, etc.
A three-dimensional work of art, usually representing a person or animal, usually created by sculpting, carving, molding, or casting.
A person or animal's natural height when standing upright.
A situation or state of affairs.
The state of things; the way things are, as opposed to the way they could be; the existing state of affairs.
Dependable, loyal, reliable, trustworthy.
One of the bars or rounds of a rack, rungs of a ladder, etc; one of the cylindrical bars of a lantern wheel
(poetry) A metrical portion; a stanza; a staff.
A highly toxic, perennial plant with purple flowers (Staphisagria macrosperma, syn. Delphinium staphisagria).
Restraint of passion; prudence; moderation; caution; steadiness; sobriety.
(intransitive) To remain in a particular place, especially for a definite or short period of time; sojourn; abide.
(intransitive, copulative) To continue to have a particular quality.
(transitive, obsolete) To remain for the purpose of; to stay to take part in or be present at (a meal, ceremony etc.).
To spend a night at someone else's home.
(obsolete) A place, or spot, in general. [10th–16th c.]
(obsolete) An estate, a property with its grounds; a farm; a homestead. [14th–19th c.]
(obsolete) To help, support, benefit or assist; to be helpful.
Smooth and not bumpy or with obstructions.
Regular and even.
beefsteak, a slice of beef, broiled or cut for broiling.
The act of stealing.
(transitive) To take illegally, or without the owner's permission, something owned by someone else without intending to return it.
(transitive, baseball) To advance safely to (another base) during the delivery of a pitch, without the aid of a hit, walk, passed ball, wild pitch, or defensive indifference.
(transitive) To get or effect surreptitiously or artfully.
(transitive) To draw attention unexpectedly in (an entertainment), especially by being the outstanding performer. Usually used in the phrase steal the show.
(intransitive) To move silently or secretly.
The suspended condensate (cloud) formed by water vapour when it encounters colder air
Pressurized water vapour used for heating, cooking, or to provide mechanical energy.
(figuratively) Internal energy for progress or motive power.
(figuratively) Pent-up anger.

cit.quote: 蒸汽机车 / 蒸汽機車

sense.def: (rail) A locomotive, usually for use on a railway, that is powered by steam.
A boat or vessel propelled by steam power.
A vessel in which articles are subjected to the action of steam, as in washing and in various processes of manufacture.
A ship or vessel propelled by steam power.
Warm and humid; full of steam.
(fatty acid) octadecanoic acid; the most common saturated fatty acid; it is found in all animal and most vegetable oils and fats; it is used in the manufacture of soap etc.
(archaic, poetic) A stallion, especially in the sense of mount.
(countable, uncountable) An artificial metal produced from iron, harder and more elastic than elemental iron; used figuratively as a symbol of hardness.
(transitive, middle voice) To soak or wet thoroughly.
(intransitive, figurative) To imbue with something; to be deeply immersed in.
To make tea (or other beverage) by placing leaves in hot water.
A tall tower, often on a church, normally topped with a spire.
The castrated male of cattle, especially one raised for beef production.
(intransitive) To guide the course of a vessel, vehicle, aircraft etc. (by means of a device such as a rudder, paddle, or steering wheel).
(transitive) To guide the course of a vessel, vehicle, aircraft etc. (by means of a device such as a rudder, paddle, or steering wheel).
(intransitive) To be directed and governed; to take a direction, or course; to obey the helm.
Equipment used to control direction; something used to steer.
A wheel-shaped control that is rotated by the driver to steer, existing in most modern land vehicles.
Any of several extinct herbivorous dinosaurs, of the suborder Stegosauria, having two rows of bony plates along the back. [from c. 1900]
(architecture, archaeology, obsolete) An acroterion, the decoration on the ridge of an ancient Greek building such as a temple.
(astronomy, notcomp) Of, pertaining to, or characteristic of stars.
A slender supporting member of an individual part of a plant such as a flower or a leaf; also, by analogy, the shaft of a feather.
(nautical) The vertical or nearly vertical forward extension of the keel, to which the forward ends of the planks or strakes are attached.
(transitive) To stop, hinder (for instance, a river or blood).
(medicine, cytology) A primal undifferentiated cell from which a variety of other cells can develop through the process of cellular differentiation.
A process for removing the inflexional, and sometimes derivational, affixes from words.
a strong foul smell; a stink.
A rest, or one of a set of rests, for the foot in ascending or descending, as a stair, or a rung of a ladder.
A running board where passengers step to get on and off the bus.
The space passed over by one movement of the foot in walking or running.
A small space or distance.
(machines) One of a series of offsets, or parts, resembling the steps of stairs, as one of the series of parts of a cone pulley on which the belt runs.
A print of the foot; a footstep; a footprint; track.
(intransitive) To move the foot in walking; to advance or recede by raising and moving one of the feet to another resting place, or by moving both feet in succession.
(intransitive) To walk; to go on foot; especially, to walk a little distance.
(intransitive, figuratively) To move mentally; to go in imagination.
(idiomatic) To resign from office; to abdicate.

(football) A dribbling move, or feint, in football (soccer), used to fool a defensive player into thinking the offensive player, in possession of the ball, in which the foot is moved over the ball without making contact with it.
(transitive, idiomatic) To increase, augment, or advance, especially by one or more steps.
The child of one's spouse but not one's own.
The daughter of one's spouse and not of oneself.
(in the narrow sense) A husband of one's biological mother after her initial marriage to or relationship with one's biological father.
The wife of one's biological father, other than one's biological mother.
One's parent's spouse who is not one's biological parent.
The grasslands of Eastern Europe and Asia. Similar to (North American) prairie and (African) savanna. [from 1671]
A vast, cold, dry grass-plain.
(idiomatic) Something used as a way to progress to something or somewhere else.

(geometry) In the International System of Units, the derived unit of solid angle; the solid angle subtended at the centre of a sphere of radius r by a portion of the surface of the sphere that has area r2. Symbol: sr
Of sound, music, etc, recorded in stereo.
(by extension) Any object or device equipped with audio components that reproduces sound in stereo, such as a stereo console in the home.
(printing, colloquial) A stereotype.
(transitive) To make a stereotype of someone or something, or characterize someone by a stereotype.
(uncomparable) Unable to reproduce (or procreate).
Germless; free from all living or viable microorganisms.
(transitive) To make unable to produce; to make unprofitable.

(transitive, biology) To kill, deactivate (denature), or destroy (break apart) all living, viable microorganisms and spores on a surface, in a fluid, or contained in a compound, such as culture media or a medical product.
A smaller, common Eurasian sturgeon, of the species Acipenser ruthenus.
Having a hardness and severity of nature or manner.
(nautical) The rear part or after end of a ship or vessel.

(biochemistry, organic compound) A class of organic compounds having a structure of 17 carbon atoms arranged in four rings; they are lipids, and occur naturally as sterols, bile acids, adrenal and sex hormones, and some vitamins; many drugs are synthetic steroids.
(medicine) A medical instrument used for listening to sounds produced within the body.
A dockworker involved in loading and unloading cargo, or in supervising such work. [from 18th c.]
(intransitive, figuratively) To suffer under uncomfortably hot conditions.
A pot used for making stew, usually large and heavy.
A cane or walking stick (usually wooden, metal or plastic) to aid in walking.
A relatively long, thin piece of wood, of any size.
(transitive) To place, set down (quickly or carelessly).
(transitive) To press (something with a sharp point) into something else.
(dated, transitive) To bring to a halt; to stymie; to puzzle.
(transitive, slang, dated) To impose upon; to compel to pay; sometimes, to cheat.
A command stereotypically given by robbers, particularly when pointing a gun: Put your hands in the air! Surrender!
Any of various insects of the order Phasmida that mimic sticks or twigs.
Something or someone that sticks (pierces, or adheres).
An adhesive label or decal.
A wooden strip placed between courses of lumber to allow air circulation and to create a gap so the unit can be picked up with a forklift (also kiln sticker).
Tending to stick; able to adhere via the drying of a viscous substance.
(finance) Tending to stay the same; resistant to change.
(Internet, of a website) Compelling enough to keep visitors from leaving.
(of an, object) Rigid; hard to bend; inflexible.
(figurative, of, _, policies and rules and their application and enforcement) Inflexible; rigid.
(slang) A cadaver; a dead person.
Discomfort or pain when trying to turn or move the neck.
Rigidity or a measure of rigidity.
Inflexibility or a measure of inflexibility.
A mark of infamy or disgrace.
A scar or birthmark.
(Christianity, chiefly, _, in the plural, _, stigmata) A mark on the body corresponding to one of the wounds of the Crucifixion on Jesus' body, and sometimes reported to bleed periodically.
A woman's shoe with a tall, slender heel (called a stiletto heel).
A heel of a shoe that is very high and narrow, at least 10 centimeters (4 inches).
(aspect) Up to a time, as in the preceding time.
(degree) To an even greater degree. Used to modify comparative adjectives or adverbs.
(painting) A work of art depicting an arrangement of inanimate objects.
A person with a calm appearance has, or may have, considerable inner emotion, character, or intellect.
Either of two poles with footrests that allow someone to stand or walk above the ground; used mostly by entertainers.
(figuratively) Elevated or raised in a contrived or unnatural way; stiff and artificially formal or pompous; also, depending on redundant, unnecessary elements.
(pharmaceutical drug) A substance that acts to increase physiological or nervous activity in the body.
Something that promotes activity, interest, or enthusiasm.
Having a manner that stimulates.
An external phenomenon that has an influence on a system, by triggering or modifying an internal phenomenon; for example, a spur or incentive that drives a person to take action or change behaviour.
(physiology, psychology, medicine) Something external that elicits or influences a physiological or psychological activity or response, or that affects any of the sensory apparatuses.
A pointed portion of an insect or arachnid used for attack.
Unwilling to spend, give, or share; ungenerous; mean
A strong bad smell.
(intransitive) To have a strong bad smell.
Having a pungent smell.
Having a strong, unpleasant smell; stinking.
A period of time spent doing or being something; a spell.
(archaic) A regular fixed payment made to someone (especially a clergyman, judge, soldier, or teacher) for services provided by them; a salary. [from Template:SAFESUBST: c.]
Public disturbance or commotion; tumultuous disorder; seditious uproar.
(transitive, dated) To change the place of in any manner; to move.
(transitive) To mix (ingredients) by stirring.
(transitive) To fry quickly in hot oil whilst constantly stirring, especially in a wok or similar pan.
A single pass of a needle in sewing; the loop or turn of the thread thus made.
An arrangement of stitches in sewing, or method of stitching in some particular way or style.
An arrangement of stitches in knitting, or method of knitting in some particular way or style.
A local sharp pain (anywhere); an acute pain, like the piercing of a needle.
Random, randomly determined.
Farm or ranch animals; livestock.
(finance) The capital raised by a company through the issue of shares. The total of shares held by an individual shareholder.
(cooking, uncountable, countable) Broth made from meat (originally bones) or vegetables, used as a basis for stew or soup.
A piece of black cloth worn under a clerical collar.
(firearm) The part of a rifle or shotgun that rests against the shooter's shoulder.
A pigeon of species Columba oenas, found in much of Europe, in the family Columbidae of pigeons and doves).
A building that trades stocks in of companies for money and vice versa.
An organisation that trades stocks in of companies for money and vice versa.

(finance) A person who buys and sells shares (stock) on a stock exchange on behalf of clients. May also provide investment advice and/or company information, depending on the level of service offered (or chosen by the client).
A broad ring of a different fur colour on the lower part of the leg of a quadruped.
A supply (especially a large one) of something kept for future use, specifically in case the cost of the item increases or if there a shortage.
(plurale tantum) A device, similar to a pillory, formerly used for public humiliation and punishment.
(of food) Having a thick, semi-solid consistency; glutinous; heavy on the stomach.
Of, or relating to stoichiometry.
(transitive, obsolete) To poke, pierce, thrust.
An organ in animals that stores food in the process of digestion.
A deliberate heavy footfall; a stamp.
(transitive, slang) To severely beat someone physically or figuratively.
(transitive) To crush grapes with one's feet to make wine
(uncountable) A hard earthen substance that can form large rocks.
A small piece of stone, a pebble.
(medicine) A hard, stone-like deposit.
(slang) High on drugs, especially cannabis.
(figuratively) Of a person, lacking warmth and emotion.
A secret informant for police.
(now, chiefly, dialectal, Scotland) A seat with a back; a chair.
(dated) A close-stool; a seat used for urination and defecation: a chamber pot, commode, outhouse seat, or toilet.
(slang, obsolete) A decoy used in a crooked gambling game.
A (usually marked) place where buses, trams or trains halt to let passengers get on and off, usually smaller than a station.
A symbol used for purposes of punctuation and representing a pause or separating clauses, particularly a full stop, comma, colon or semicolon.
(intransitive) Not to continue.
(transitive) To cause (something) to cease moving or progressing.
(transitive) To cause (something) to come to an end.
(intransitive) To stay; to spend a short time; to reside or tarry temporarily.
A building for keeping goods of any kind, especially provisions.
One who runs a shop, either the owner or manager.
A room used for storage.
A floor or level of a building or ship.
A large wading bird with long legs and a long beak of the family Ciconiidae.

A slight coloring.
A color considered with reference to other very similar colors.
Very small.

A gratuity; a small amount of money left for a bartender, waiter, taxi driver or other servant as a token of appreciation. [from mid-18th c.]
(idiomatic) A small indication of a larger possibility; the first part encountered of a problem that is much bigger than it seems.
(countable) The wooden piece used in this game.

(intransitive) To become sleepy or weary.
(transitive) To make sleepy or weary.
(intransitive) To become bored or impatient (with).
In need of some rest or sleep.
The state of being tired.
Causing fatigue or boredom; wearisome.
That tires or tire.
Thin, woven, gauze-like fabric.

Any small passerine bird of the family Paridae, which are found in the woods of the Northern Hemisphere and of Africa.

(mathematics) Indicating an exponent.
To achieve the previously specified goal.

Any of several European plants, of the genus Linaria, having two-lipped yellow flowers.

In the current era; nowadays; these days.

Labour, work, especially of a grueling nature.

Receptacle designed to receive the dejections of humans.
Paper, usually on a roll, to clean oneself after defecation, or to pat oneself dry after urination.
Requiring continuous physical effort; laborious.

Something serving as an expression of something else.

The male of the domesticated cat, especially if not neutered.
The male of certain other animals.
A widely cultivated plant, Solanum lycopersicum, having edible fruit.

A small building (or "vault") for the remains of the dead, with walls, a roof, and (if it is to be used for more than one corpse) a door. It may be partly or wholly in the ground (except for its entrance) in a cemetery, or it may be inside a church proper or in its crypt. Single tombs may be permanently sealed; those for families (or other groups) have doors for access whenever needed.
A girl who behaves in a typically boyish manner.
A grave marker, a stone slab or similar object marking a person's grave.
One in a series of volumes.
A large or scholarly book.
Imaging by sections or sectioning.
On the day after the present day.
(uncountable) The day after the present day.
Any of various units of mass, originally notionally equal to the contents of a tun, particularly:
(figuratively) Any large, excessive, or overwhelming amount of anything.
(music) (in a Gregorian chant) A recitational melody.
(linguistics) The pitch of a word that distinguishes a difference in meaning, for example in Chinese.
(dated) A whining style of speaking; a kind of mournful or artificial strain of voice; an affected speaking with a measured rhythm and a regular rise and fall of the voice.
(linguistics) A phoneme in a language that uses different tones for different meanings.
(mostly plural) An instrument or tool used for manipulating things in a fire without touching them with the hands.

An instrument or tool used for picking things up without touching them with the hands or fingers, consisting of two slats or grips hinged at the end or in the middle, and sometimes including a spring to open the grips.
(countable, uncountable) This organ, as taken from animals used for food (especially cows).
In a shoe, the flap of material that goes between the laces and the foot (so called because it resembles a tongue in the mouth).
The fish Cynoglossus semilaevis.
A phrase that is deliberately designed to be difficult to say correctly, usually because of varying combinations of similar phonemes.
A carbonated beverage containing quinine, originally used as a prophylactic against malaria, and now used as a soft drink or as a mixer in gin and tonic and other cocktails.

(anatomy, immunology) Ellipsis of palatine tonsil.

sense.def: (pathology) Inflammation of the tonsils.
The hairstyle and characteristic bald patch resulting from being tonsured.

(degree) To an excessive degree; over; more than enough.
(idiomatic) That's a pity.

Excessive (used with countable nouns).

Any mechanical device meant to ease or do a task.
Any piece of equipment used in a profession, e.g. a craftman's tools.

A set of tools kept together, especially comprising all the tools suitable for some particular type of work.
(informal) A cartoon, especially an animated television show.
(by extension, informal) A fart; flatus.
(idiomatic) To promote oneself; to boast or brag; to tout oneself.
A sharp projection on the blade of a saw or similar implement.

(LGBT, _, slang) A man, trans woman, or other person with a penis, who penetrates or has a preference for penetrating during intercourse with other people with penises.
A man's formal hat, with a tall cylindrical crown (often of silk).
(idiomatic) Very good; of the highest level or quality. [from 1848]

An often clear, yellowish-brown gemstone cut from this.

Subject; theme; a category or general area of interest.

(linguistics, sociolinguistics) The speech form, variety (lect) of a particular place or region.

(less common) A word derived from the name of a place.

A tightly braided necklace or collar, often made of metal, worn by various early European peoples.

A rich, dense cake, typically made with many eggs and relatively little flour (as opposed to a sponge cake or gâteau).
