Any of various land-dwelling reptiles, of the family Testudinidae (chiefly, North America) or the order Testudines (chiefly, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, South Africa, India) , whose body is enclosed in a shell (carapace plus plastron). The animal can withdraw its head and four legs partially into the shell, providing some protection from predators.
Made of the covering of carapace of hawksbill turtle.
The horny, translucent, mottled covering of the carapace of the hawksbill turtle, used as a veneer etc.
Any of several butterflies, mostly of the genera Nymphalis and Aglais that have similar markings.

In relation to (someone or something).
For the purpose of attaining (an aim).

One who earns a living by trading goods or securities.
A skilled manual worker (implied male).

A collectible card, sometimes sticker, usually made out of paperboard or thick paper, which usually contains an image of a certain person, place or thing (fictional or real) and a short description of the picture, along with other text (attacks, statistics, or trivia). There is a wide variation of different types of cards, like sports, cars, natural history, film characters or other information of interest to purchasers. Sometimes is included with tobacco, food or confectionery products.

A situation in which road traffic accumulates until it is stationary or very slow.

A sign for the control of traffic or the information of drivers.

A drama or similar work, in which the main character is brought to ruin or otherwise suffers the extreme consequences of some tragic flaw or weakness of character.
The genre of such works, and the art of producing them.

Causing great sadness or suffering.
Relating to tragedy in a literary work.

A group of animals, vehicles, or people that follow one another in a line, such as a wagon train; a caravan or procession. [from 15th c.]

A similar vehicle for carrying materials.

To entangle, as in a net.

(countable) A dazed or unconscious condition.

(slang, chiefly, derogatory, offensive) A transsexual, transgender, or transvestite person, usually a trans woman.
Free from emotional or mental disturbance.
Calm; without motion or sound.
Transgender or transsexual.

(of a communications device) To both transmit and receive
(mathematics) any irrational number that is not an algebraic number
Something which has been transcribed; a writing or composition consisting of the same words as the original; a written copy.
A written version of what was said orally

In Gothic churches these project greatly, and should be called the arms of the transept. It is common, however, to speak of the arms themselves as the transepts.
(transitive) To move or pass from one place, person or thing to another.
(transitive) To convey the impression of (something) from one surface to another.
(intransitive) To be or become transferred.
(transitive, legal) To arrange for something to belong to or be officially controlled by somebody else.
(intransitive) To undergo a transformation; to change in appearance or character.
The act of transforming or the state of being transformed.

(mathematics) The replacement of the variables in an algebraic expression by their values in terms of another set of variables; a mapping of one space onto another or onto itself; a function that changes the position or direction of the axes of a coordinate system.
(linguistics) A rule that systematically converts one syntactic form into another; a sentence derived by such a rule.
(genetics) The alteration of a bacterial cell caused by the transfer of DNA from another, especially if pathogenic.

Remaining for only a brief time.

(astronomy) The passage of a celestial body or other object across the observer's meridian, or across the disk of a larger celestial body.
The conveyance of people or goods from one place to another, especially on a public transportation system; the vehicles used for such conveyance.
A surveying instrument rather like a theodolite that measures horizontal and vertical angles.
The process of change from one form, state, style or place to another.
(LGBT) The process or act of changing from one gender role to another, or of bringing one's outward appearance in line with one's internal gender identity.
Making a transit or passage.
(grammar, of a verb) Taking a direct object or objects.
(set theory, of a relation on a set) Having the property that if an element a is related to b and b is related to c, then a is necessarily related to c.

Consequently, transitive verbs can also be used in the passive voice when the direct object of the equivalent active-voice sentence becomes the subject.

It corresponds to the archaic English particle "O" as used in solemn or poetic address e.g.: Hear me, O Albion! Languages that regularly employ the vocative include Arabic, Bengali, Bulgarian, Czech, Georgian, Greek, Hawaiian, Hindi-Urdu, Irish, Latin, Latvian, Lithuanian, Ojibwe, Polish, Romanian, Ruthenian/Rusyn, Sanskrit, Scottish Gaelic, Serbo-Croatian, Slovak, Tamil and Ukrainian.

A means of overcoming some obstacle, especially an obstacle consisting of constraints, or laws or regulations.

A person who performs labor for a living, especially manual labor.
All the workers employed by a specific organization or state, or on a specific project.

A man who labours for wages.
The place where someone works.
A brief, intensive course of education for a small group, emphasizing interaction and practical problem solving.
An academic conference.

(countable, medicine) A general medical examination to assess a person's health and fitness.

An individual or group perspective or social setting.
(computing) The part of an operating system distributed with the kernel, consisting of the shell and other programs.
A map of a world; a cartographic representation, a projection done to scale, representative of a planet's surface.
A particular structure that manages the world's stability, informed by a number of legal, political and socio-economic factors.
The ideology of universal global understanding and non-violence.
A nation or state so powerful that it can influence world affairs.
